invariants: The conditions are evaluated against the version being copied, not against a version observed earlier (internal/storage/store.go:90-97).
The destination is a new publication: it gets its own version id and its own last-modified time (internal/storage/memory_copy.go:59-74).
The source metadata travels with the bytes: content type, metadata and checksum fields are copied, not re-derived (internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:63-73).
A copy is refused if the source or the destination bucket does not exist (internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:36-41, internal/storage/workspace/objects.go:227-229).
The four names are validated in a fixed order so that the answer does not depend on which end a store checks first (internal/storage/preconditions.go:29-40).
error_modes: storage.ErrPreconditionFailed when a condition does not hold (internal/storage/preconditions.go:49, :51, :56).
storage.ErrBucketNotFound when either bucket is absent, and storage.ErrObjectNotFound when the source key is absent (internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:36-47).
storage.ErrInvalidBucketName and storage.ErrInvalidKey for malformed names (internal/storage/preconditions.go:30-39).
storage.ErrRecoveryHeld when a recovery hold covers the destination (internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:76-78).
storage.ErrMutationCommitted when the local copy landed but a later propagation step failed (internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:264).
ordering: The conditions must be checked before the destination is published; a refused copy propagates nothing (internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:224-226).
In run-through mode the outbox entry for the destination is written before the local copy and committed after it (internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:237-269).
The filesystem backend settles its save journal before the copy (internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:32-34).
The source must exist before the destination is written: both adapters read the source first and publish second (internal/storage/memory_copy.go:40-56, internal/storage/workspace/objects.go:242-254).
configuration: Whether the guarantee applies is decided by a type assertion at the point of use, not by configuration (internal/s3api/copy.go:85, internal/runtime/objects.go:320, internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:277).
In run-through mode the copy's upstream behaviour depends on the write policy resolved from the configuration (internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:230).

implementation: The interface itself is one method; the behaviour lives in five implementations. storage.MemoryStore captures the source and commits the destination under one lock (internal/storage/memory_copy.go:32-78). fs.FilesystemStore opens the source record under the same lock it holds for the destination write, refuses when a recovery hold covers the destination and streams the source bytes into the new record (internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:25-84). workspace.Store resolves the source path, reads the file and publishes the destination under one lock (internal/storage/workspace/objects.go:223-260). runthrough.Adapter decides whether the destination is propagated upstream, prepares an outbox entry, then delegates the copy to the local store and commits the intent (internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:227-271). runtime.StoreAdapter routes the request through the runtime instance so quota and authority are enforced (internal/runtime/adapter.go:155-161).

callers.scope: the S3 copy handler: it hands the source conditions to the store when the store can evaluate them, and otherwise falls back to head-then-check-then-copy at :94-103.
the run-through adapter: it delegates to the local store, or checks an observed source version and then copies.
the runtime instance: it delegates to the store, or performs an unchecked copy.
the runtime's capability probe, which decides whether the runtime itself must evaluate the copy's source conditions.
the contract suite: every backing store must implement the interface, and the assertion at :179 requires a stale If-Match to be refused with storage.ErrPreconditionFailed.

depth_assessment.deletion_test: Delete storage.ConditionalCopyStore and the atomicity rule does not vanish - it moves. Every one of the five implementations would have to fold the source-condition evaluation into its ordinary CopyObject, the S3 layer would lose the branch at internal/s3api/copy.go:85 and the runtime would lose the branch at internal/runtime/objects.go:320, and the two fallback paths would silently become the only paths. The interface is where the 'conditions and bytes come from one version' rule is stated once, and the contract suite at internal/storage/copy_contract_test.go:142 is what holds the implementations to it.

leverage: A caller gets one answer about whether a copy is atomic with respect to its source conditions, and the S3 layer and the runtime can both delegate instead of each re-implementing a head-then-check-then-copy window. The contract suite at internal/storage/copy_contract_test.go:142 asserts the guarantee for all three backing stores registered in backendFactories, so a new backend added to that list must satisfy it rather than inventing a new test.
locality: The rule lives in internal/storage/store.go:86-100; the shared evaluation lives in internal/storage/preconditions.go:46; the five implementations live in internal/storage/memory_copy.go, internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go, internal/storage/workspace/objects.go, internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go and internal/runtime/adapter.go. The two fallbacks live in internal/s3api/copy.go:94-103 and internal/runtime/objects.go:309-324 - a change to the guarantee has to be made in six places plus the contract test.
risks: The guarantee is not visible in the type system: internal/s3api/copy.go:85 and internal/runtime/objects.go:320 both branch on a type assertion, so a store that stops implementing the interface silently loses atomicity rather than failing to compile.

The embedded adapter for caller-supplied stores (internal/embedded/store.go:291-308) is the one production adapter that does not implement it, so the public library's caller-supplied store gets the weaker head-then-copy guarantee while the internal backends do not - a difference a caller cannot control from the public API, which exposes no conditional-copy opt-in.

All of the fallback paths are the same weaker shape - check the conditions against a head observed earlier, then copy unconditionally - so they are equivalent in guarantee: internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:280-289 (only when conditions were supplied), internal/runtime/objects.go:280-286 together with storeCopy at :319-324, and internal/s3api/copy.go:94-103 (which re-checks the request headers). None of them can make the check and the copied bytes the same version.

The run-through adapter's outbox writes the destination either way (internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:224-226), so a refused copy depends on the local store's own precondition failure arriving before anything is prepared.

priority.rationale: The blast radius is bounded - five implementations and three call sites - but the coupling is hidden: the guarantee a client gets is decided by a runtime type assertion, so a backend change can quietly weaken copy atomicity for every S3 client without any test failing, because the contract suite only covers the three backing stores. It is not P1 because the contract suite pins those three to the strong behaviour and the shared evaluator in internal/storage/preconditions.go:46 gives one place to change the rule.

next_action: Make the capability explicit rather than a bare type assertion, so the choice is visible at the call site: add a method to storage.ConditionalCopyStore that reports whether the implementation evaluates the conditions on the version it copies, and have internal/s3api/copy.go:85 and internal/runtime/objects.go:320 consult it explicitly rather than inferring it from the assertion succeeding. The concrete interface that should change is storage.ConditionalCopyStore at internal/storage/store.go:98, and embedded.storeAdapter at internal/embedded/store.go should either implement it or state in its doc comment that a caller-supplied store permanently gets the weaker guarantee.

title: storage.RecoveryHoldStore has one production adapter, so it is not a seam
claimed_root_cause: Candidate: a third optional seam at internal/storage/recovery.go:29, where a store that can pin the bytes one caller observed is discovered by type assertion so the runtime can refuse writes over held objects.

trace.scope: Instance.BeginObjectRecoveryHold is the exported entry that begins a hold through the bound store
the runtime discovers the capability by asserting the bound store to storage.RecoveryHoldStore and asking SupportsRecoveryHolds
the filesystem backend's BeginRecoveryHold, the only production implementation of the interface

evidence.detail: the interface: SupportsRecoveryHolds, BeginRecoveryHold and ReleaseRecoveryHold, with five sentinels declared beside it at :8-17.
the only production implementation of SupportsRecoveryHolds; a repository-wide search for func (X) SupportsRecoveryHolds() bool finds no other store.
the only production implementation of BeginRecoveryHold.
the only production implementation of ReleaseRecoveryHold.
the runtime's discovery by type assertion; the interface is asserted at :24, :37 and :72, and a store without it gets storage.ErrRecoveryHoldsUnsupported at :39 and :74.

the near-miss: workspace.Registry.AdmitRecoveryHold is a registry-level hold over a workspace capture, with the signature (RecoveryHoldRequest, string) rather than (context.Context, storage.RecoveryHoldOptions); it does not satisfy storage.RecoveryHoldStore and a search of internal/storage/workspace for SupportsRecoveryHolds, BeginRecoveryHold and ReleaseRecoveryHold returns no matches.
adaptStore wraps a caller-supplied store in storeAdapter, which carries none of the recovery-hold methods, so the public substitution path cannot supply a second adapter.
runtime.StoreAdapter implements storage.Store by delegating to an Instance but defines none of the three recovery-hold methods, so it is not a second adapter either.
the public test asserts that a memory store (stow.Open) advertises no recovery holds, confirming the capability is filesystem-only at the public surface.

reason: One production adapter and no extension story: fs.FilesystemStore is the only implementation of all three methods, confirmed by a repository-wide search for the three method names (only fs.FilesystemStore, plus the runtime facades embedded.Runtime and runtime.Instance, which implement SupportsRecoveryHolds alone and are not store adapters). The one candidate second adapter, workspace.Registry.AdmitRecoveryHold (internal/storage/workspace/recovery_hold_mutation.go:13), is a different concept with a different signature - a registry-level hold over a workspace capture rather than a store-level hold over object bytes - and it does not satisfy storage.RecoveryHoldStore; the workspace package defines none of the interface's methods. The public substitution path is closed: embedded.adaptStore (internal/embedded/store.go:120) produces a storeAdapter with no recovery-hold methods, and runtime.StoreAdapter (internal/runtime/adapter.go:15) carries none either. The deletion test disqualifies it: delete the interface and the hold journal stays inside fs (internal/storage/fs/recovery_holds.go:54-60) while the runtime's two refusals become direct calls to the one implementation; no complexity concentrates in a substitutable place. An interface with exactly one adapter is a hypothetical seam.

title: storage.SaveRequestStore has one production adapter, so it is not a seam
claimed_root_cause: Candidate: a second optional seam at internal/storage/save_requests.go:24, where a store that can journal a save request is discovered by type assertion so the runtime can replay a write whose outcome was lost.

trace.scope: Instance.SaveObject is the exported entry that, for a nonempty RequestKey, replays the request through the bound store at :105 before writing

the runtime discovers the capability by asserting the bound store to storage.SaveRequestStore and asking SupportsDurableSaveRequests; the dispatch to ReplaySaveRequest is at :24 and to ResolveSaveRequest at :71
the filesystem backend's ReplaySaveRequest, the only production implementation of the interface

evidence.detail: the interface: SupportsDurableSaveRequests, ReplaySaveRequest and ResolveSaveRequest, with seven sentinels declared beside it at :8-16.
the only production implementation of ReplaySaveRequest.
the only production implementation of ResolveSaveRequest.
the only production implementation of SupportsDurableSaveRequests; it is true only on darwin and linux (:46-49).
the runtime's discovery by type assertion; the interface is asserted at :13, :24 and :71, and a store without it gets storage.ErrSaveRequestsUnsupported at :69.
lostSaveReplyStore is a test-only implementation, in a _test.go file, and does not count as a production adapter.
embedded.Runtime.SupportsDurableSaveRequests delegates to the inner runtime instance; it defines neither ReplaySaveRequest nor ResolveSaveRequest, so it is not a substitutable store.

adaptStore wraps a caller-supplied store in storeAdapter (or storeWithStaging/storeWithMultipart), which carries none of the save-request methods and does not type-assert the caller's store for the capability, so the public substitution path cannot supply a second adapter.
runtime.StoreAdapter implements storage.Store by delegating to an Instance but defines none of the three save-request methods, so it is not a second adapter either.

the public-surface test asserts that a memory store, the workspace backend and a supplied-runtime store all refuse a keyed save with stow.ErrSaveRequestsUnsupported and that Capabilities().DurableSaveRequests is false, confirming the capability is filesystem-only at the public surface.

reason: One production adapter and no extension story. A repository-wide search for the three method names finds exactly one store that implements all of them: fs.FilesystemStore (ReplaySaveRequest internal/storage/fs/save_requests.go:26, ResolveSaveRequest :80, SupportsDurableSaveRequests internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:49). The other two types that define a method of the same name are not substitutable stores: lostSaveReplyStore (internal/runtime/save_requests_test.go:19) is a test fake in a _test.go file, and embedded.Runtime (internal/embedded/save_requests.go:20) delegates SupportsDurableSaveRequests to the inner runtime instance and defines neither ReplaySaveRequest nor ResolveSaveRequest. runtime.StoreAdapter (internal/runtime/adapter.go:15) implements storage.Store by delegating to an Instance but carries none of the three methods, so it is not a second adapter either. The public substitution path is closed: embedded.adaptStore (internal/embedded/store.go:120) wraps a caller-supplied embedded.Store in storeAdapter (or storeWithStaging/storeWithMultipart), which forwards none of the save-request methods and does not type-assert the caller's store for the capability, so a caller-supplied store can never reach the runtime as a storage.SaveRequestStore; pkg/stow/save_requests_test.go:235 asserts this at the public surface (memory, workspace and supplied-runtime all refuse with stow.ErrSaveRequestsUnsupported and Capabilities().DurableSaveRequests is false). The deletion test disqualifies the seam: delete storage.SaveRequestStore and the complexity stays where it already lives - the journal, the request-key meaning hash and the settle logic in internal/storage/fs/save_requests.go:15-274 - while the runtime's dispatch at internal/runtime/save_requests.go:23-33 collapses into a direct call to the one implementation that exists; no complexity concentrates in a substitutable place. An interface with exactly one adapter and no extension story is a hypothetical seam.

title: storage.Store — the core object-model contract and its optional capability interfaces
summary: storage.Store is the platform-neutral object-model contract of stow-s3: twelve methods covering four bucket operations, seven object operations and Close (internal/storage/store.go:13-40). It fixes what an object is — buckets, objects, a continuation-token list with common prefixes, multipart upload descriptors, ETag and checksum rules, write preconditions — and nothing else. Multipart is deliberately not a member (internal/storage/store.go:8-12); it and ten other capabilities are optional interfaces that a caller discovers by type assertion at the point of use: storage.MultipartStore (internal/storage/store.go:48), storage.ConditionalCopyStore (:98), storage.UsageRevisionStore (:104), storage.PutChecksumStore (:109), storage.ObjectUsageStore (:116), storage.GuardedWriteStore (internal/storage/guarded.go:12), storage.SaveRequestStore (internal/storage/save_requests.go:24), storage.RecoveryHoldStore (internal/storage/recovery.go:29), storage.RangeStore (internal/storage/range.go:13), storage.StagedWriteStore (internal/storage/staged.go:13) and storage.QuotaStoreProvider (internal/storage/commit.go:19). The package also carries the rules the model is made of — bucket and key validation, the quoted-MD5 ETag and its multipart composite form, the five checksum digests and the verify/compute decision, the If-Match grammar, the three pagination algorithms, the 5 MiB minimum part size — plus one in-memory backend. It is consumed by the S3 HTTP surface, the embedded runtime, the run-through adapter, the embedded public library and the CLI, and it is implemented by nine concrete types.

trace.scope: an S3 PUT arrives at the HTTP surface; the handler materialises the body once, verifies Content-MD5 and the requested checksum, and prepares the PutOptions

the call into the contract: s.store.PutObject(ctx, bucket, key, takeRequestBody(r, body), storage.PutOptions{...}) — content type, user metadata, checksum algorithm and value, If-Match and If-None-Match
FilesystemStore.PutObject, one of the nine implementations of the contract, stages the write and then commits it
the staged commit publishes the record only after the precondition, write-guard and recovery-hold checks have run against the current version
atomicfile.WriteStream writes the object record — version, ETag, content type, metadata, checksum and payload — to the store's bucket directory on disk

evidence.detail: the twelve-method core interface: CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, HeadBucket, ListBuckets, PutObject, GetObject, HeadObject, DeleteObject, DeleteObjects, CopyObject, ListObjectsV2, Close
the stated reason multipart is not a member: requiring it of every store would put one protocol's streaming shape into the object model
DeleteObjects' contract in prose: a key that was not there counts as confirmed, only a key whose delete failed is left out, and on failure the keys confirmed before the failure are returned
CopyObject's contract in prose: it publishes the destination key from exactly one version, so a concurrent write cannot be half-copied
why storage.ConditionalCopyStore is separately optional: a store that does not implement it can only promise an internally coherent copy, which is strictly weaker and observable by the client
MultipartUpload carries the properties fixed at initiation, so a caller reconciling in-flight uploads can answer from the upload itself rather than asking the store to remember
PaginateObjects is the one ListObjectsV2 algorithm: common prefixes count against MaxKeys and truncation happens on the logical entry, so every backend truncates identically
CompletionETag keeps a single-part completion's own ETag and only applies the composite '-N' digest to a genuinely multipart object, because a client returns that value on its next conditional write
VerifyChecksum is package-level precisely because verifying an integrity claim is part of the object model; supplying an algorithm without a value is an error rather than a silent pass
ETagHeaderMatches implements the If-Match/If-None-Match grammar inside the store, including weak validators, comma-separated lists and '*'
MinPartSize is 5 MiB, the S3 rule, and it lives in the contract package rather than in each backend
the sentinel vocabulary the whole system agrees on: bucket, key, upload, part, precondition, checksum and capacity refusals
withStores runs one property suite against the memory, filesystem and workspace backends, so the contract is checked as a property of every backend rather than of one
the suite asserts that every backend implements storage.ConditionalCopyStore, making the optional capability a de-facto requirement of the shipped backends
the production call site of the contract: the S3 surface calls s.store.PutObject with the request's options and returns the resulting ETag
the S3 surface discovers storage.ConditionalCopyStore at the point of use and falls back to a head-then-copy, the weaker guarantee the interface documents
the embedded runtime holds the store and probes its multipart capability once at construction, re-deriving it after a store swap at :240

guardedSavesLocked discovers storage.GuardedWriteStore and checks its SupportsGuardedWrites() predicate; a store without it is refused with ErrGuardedSavesUnsupported at :143 rather than performing an unguarded write
adaptStore presents a caller-supplied public store as the internal contract and adds the optional half only when the caller's store carries it, so discovery happens rather than being declared
the CLI binds the store it built — the run-through adapter in run-through mode — into the runtime, so the runtime probes the wrapper for capabilities rather than the local store
FilesystemStore.SupportsGuardedWrites() is true only on darwin and linux, so the same concrete type carries different capabilities on different platforms

interface.types: The core interface storage.Store (internal/storage/store.go:13) is: CreateBucket(ctx, name) error; DeleteBucket(ctx, name) error; HeadBucket(ctx, name) (*BucketInfo, error); ListBuckets(ctx) ([]BucketInfo, error); PutObject(ctx, bucket, key, body io.Reader, opts PutOptions) (*ObjectMeta, error); GetObject(ctx, bucket, key) (io.ReadCloser, *ObjectMeta, error); HeadObject(ctx, bucket, key) (*ObjectMeta, error); DeleteObject(ctx, bucket, key) error; DeleteObjects(ctx, bucket, keys []string) ([]string, error); CopyObject(ctx, srcBucket, srcKey, dstBucket, dstKey) (*ObjectMeta, error); ListObjectsV2(ctx, bucket, opts ListOptions) (*ListResult, error); Close() error. The value types are ObjectMeta (internal/storage/types.go:8 — Bucket, Key, VersionID, Size, ETag, ContentType, LastModified, Metadata, ChecksumAlgorithm, ChecksumValue), BucketInfo (:22 — Name, CreationDate), PutOptions (:28 — ComputeChecksum, ContentType, Metadata, ChecksumAlgorithm, ChecksumValue, IfMatch, IfNoneMatch, Guard, RequestKey), ListOptions (:41 — Prefix, Delimiter, ContinuationToken, MaxKeys, StartAfter), ListResult (:50 — Objects, CommonPrefixes, IsTruncated, ContinuationToken, NextContinuationToken, KeyCount), MultipartUpload (:60 — UploadID, Bucket, Key, Initiated, Options), MultipartOptions (:86 — ContentType, Metadata, ChecksumAlgorithm, ChecksumValue), MultipartListOptions (:107), MultipartListResult (:115), ListPartsOptions (:128), ListPartsResult (:134) and PartInfo (:143 — PartNumber, ETag, Size, LastModified). Eleven capabilities are optional interfaces discovered by type assertion: storage.MultipartStore (internal/storage/store.go:48 — CreateMultipartUpload, GetMultipartUpload, UploadPart, CompleteMultipartUpload, AbortMultipartUpload, ListParts, ValidateMultipartUpload, ListMultipartUploads), storage.ConditionalCopyStore (:98 — CopyObjectCond(ctx, CopyRequest)), storage.UsageRevisionStore (:104 — UsageRevision(ctx) (uint64, error)), storage.PutChecksumStore (:109 — ComputesPutChecksums() bool), storage.ObjectUsageStore (:116 — ScanObjectUsage(ctx, bucket) (ObjectUsage, error)), storage.GuardedWriteStore (internal/storage/guarded.go:12 — SupportsGuardedWrites() bool), storage.SaveRequestStore (internal/storage/save_requests.go:24 — SupportsDurableSaveRequests, ReplaySaveRequest, ResolveSaveRequest), storage.RecoveryHoldStore (internal/storage/recovery.go:29 — SupportsRecoveryHolds, BeginRecoveryHold, ReleaseRecoveryHold), storage.RangeStore (internal/storage/range.go:13 — OpenObjectRange(ctx, bucket, key, ObjectRange)), storage.StagedWriteStore (internal/storage/staged.go:13 — StageObject(ctx, bucket, key, body, opts) (StagedObject, error)) and storage.QuotaStoreProvider (internal/storage/commit.go:19 — QuotaStore() Store). The write guard is WriteGuard{Absent bool, Fingerprint [32]byte} (internal/storage/guarded.go:17) and the copy request is CopyRequest{SourceBucket, SourceKey, DestBucket, DestKey, Options CopyOptions} (internal/storage/store.go:78) — a struct rather than positional parameters precisely so a source and destination cannot be swapped by accident.
invariants: Names and keys are validated before anything else happens: a bucket name is 3-63 characters of lowercase letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', may not contain '..', may not parse as an IP address and may not carry a reserved service prefix; a key is non-empty, at most 1024 bytes, valid UTF-8 and contains no NUL (internal/storage/util.go:24, :50).
A request naming a bucket that does not exist is refused before the body is read, so an impossible request costs no bytes (internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:102).

The ETag is a quoted MD5 hex of the object's bytes (internal/storage/util.go:76); a completed multipart object carries the part's own ETag when there was exactly one part and the composite '-N' digest otherwise (internal/storage/util.go:130). These two forms are not interchangeable behind the API, because a client returns the value on its next conditional write.

The checksum algorithm and the checksum value must be supplied together. A caller who supplies neither has made no claim and nothing is verified; supplying one without the other is an error rather than a silent pass (internal/storage/checksum.go:68).

A copy publishes exactly one version: the bytes and the metadata always describe the same source version, and the destination receives its own new version (internal/storage/store.go:34, internal/storage/memory_copy.go:20, internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:24, internal/storage/workspace/objects.go:220).

DeleteObjects confirms a key that was not there, because S3 deletes idempotently; only a key whose delete actually failed is left out of the returned slice (internal/storage/store.go:23, internal/storage/memory.go:289).
ListObjectsV2 counts common prefixes against MaxKeys and truncates on the logical entry, so a store truncates identically whatever protocol asks (internal/storage/util.go:309).

Metadata maps returned to a caller are independent copies of the store's state, so a caller cannot mutate a stored object through a map it kept (internal/storage/memory.go:19, internal/storage/util.go:147).
Multipart upload properties are fixed at initiation and completion publishes exactly those; no part may change them (internal/storage/types.go:65).

A completion's parts must be strictly ascending with no duplicates and at least one part, and every non-final part must be at least MinPartSize (5 MiB) — decided from stored sizes rather than from the request (internal/storage/util.go:106, internal/storage/multipart.go:29).

If-Match and If-None-Match are compared as opaque tags; the tag is trimmed of quotes, a weak validator is accepted only where the comparison is weak, and '*' matches anything (internal/storage/preconditions.go:80).
A write's preconditions and its write guard are evaluated against the same object version the write replaces (internal/storage/fs/fs_put.go:47-52, internal/storage/memory.go:180-185).
A store that can write multipart must also be able to read it back, because a consumer reconciling in-flight uploads must be able to ask what is in flight (internal/storage/store.go:42-47).
Close is called exactly once by whoever owns the store, and the runtime closes the store it was given (internal/runtime/instance.go:245).
error_modes: The sentinel vocabulary is internal/storage/errors.go:5-30: ErrBucketNotFound, ErrInvalidBucketName, ErrBucketExists, ErrObjectNotFound, ErrInvalidKey, ErrInvalidUpload, ErrInvalidPart, ErrObjectUncertain, ErrEntityTooSmall, ErrUploadNotFound, ErrNoSuchUpload, ErrPreconditionFailed, ErrChecksumMismatch, ErrMD5Mismatch, ErrBucketNotEmpty, ErrMultipartUnsupported.

ErrObjectUncertain means the store could not determine whether the object is there; reporting absence instead would lose data on a create-only write (internal/storage/errors.go:13, produced at internal/storage/workspace/absence.go:40).

Capability refusals have their own sentinels: ErrSaveRequestsUnsupported, ErrInvalidSaveRequest, ErrSaveRequestConflict, ErrSaveRequestNotFound, ErrSaveRequestNotCommitted, ErrSaveRequestUnknown, ErrSaveRequestFull (internal/storage/save_requests.go:8-16); ErrRecoveryHoldsUnsupported, ErrInvalidRecoveryHold, ErrRecoveryHoldNotFound, ErrRecoveryHoldFull, ErrRecoveryHeld (internal/storage/recovery.go:8-17); ErrSaveConflict (internal/storage/guarded.go:9).

ErrMutationCommitted means the authoritative local mutation completed but a later step failed; callers must account for the committed data while still reporting the underlying error (internal/storage/commit.go:5).

The S3 surface translates these upward through one ordered table (internal/s3api/errors.go:127) via mapStorageError (:147), with ErrMutationCommitted handled ahead of the table so a written object is never reported as a missing key.
A store that invents its own refusal instead of returning a sentinel reaches the client as an unmapped server fault rather than the intended S3 code.
ordering: A multipart upload's properties are fixed at initiation; completion publishes exactly those and no part may change them (internal/storage/types.go:65, internal/storage/multipart.go:79).
A completion's parts must be supplied in strictly ascending part-number order with no duplicates (internal/storage/util.go:106).

The precondition check and the guard check happen against the current version before the write is published, and the write is staged before it is committed (internal/storage/fs/staged_put.go:135, internal/storage/fs/fs_put.go:47).

A store that can evaluate copy-source conditions must evaluate them against the same captured version whose bytes it copies; a caller that checks the condition itself and then calls CopyObject has asked for a version the store may no longer be able to honour (internal/storage/store.go:86-97).
The runtime re-derives a store's multipart capability whenever the store is replaced, so a swapped store must be re-probed (internal/runtime/instance.go:240).
A staged write must be committed or aborted; after Commit or Abort the staged object refuses to be reused (internal/storage/fs/staged_put.go:138, internal/storage/staged.go:8).
An OwnedBody may be transferred exactly once; a second read returns errOwnedBodyTaken (internal/storage/owned_body.go:31).
configuration: None. The package reads no environment variable, config file or flag: a grep of internal/storage/*.go finds no import from the rest of the repository, and the package doc states the platform-neutral intent (internal/storage/storage.go:1-3).

The store is constructed by its caller: storage.NewMemoryStore() (internal/storage/memory.go:47), fs.NewFilesystemStore(dataDir) (internal/storage/fs/fs.go:42) or workspace.New(Options{Root, Bucket}) (internal/storage/workspace/workspace.go:72).

Capability is a property of the concrete type, and for the filesystem backend also of the operating system: SupportsGuardedWrites is true only on darwin and linux, and SupportsDurableSaveRequests and SupportsRecoveryHolds both defer to it (internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:46, :49, internal/storage/fs/recovery_holds.go:52).

The runtime's own limits are configuration of the runtime, not of the store: MaxBytes, MaxObjects and MaxMultipartUploads are supplied when the runtime is opened (internal/runtime/instance.go:34, internal/runtime/state.go:88).

implementation: The package is the contract plus the rules that implement it plus one in-memory backend. store.go declares storage.Store and five optional interfaces; guarded.go, save_requests.go, recovery.go and range.go declare the other four, and staged.go and commit.go declare storage.StagedWriteStore and storage.QuotaStoreProvider beside them. util.go holds the shared value machinery: ValidateBucketName and ValidateKey, the record-version and upload-id minters (random 16 bytes, hex), the ETag helpers (quoted MD5 for a single write, the composite '-N' digest for a completed multipart, and CompletionETag which chooses between them), the metadata cloner, and the three pagination algorithms (parts by part-number marker, multipart uploads by the (Key, Initiated, UploadID) marker pair, and objects by continuation token with common prefixes folded into the same logical sequence). checksum.go holds the five supported digests (CRC32, CRC32C, CRC64NVME, SHA1, SHA256) and the two entry points that decide them: VerifyChecksum checks a caller-supplied claim against the bytes, ResolvePutChecksum computes the digest or verifies one, and putDigest refuses an algorithm without a value. preconditions.go holds the shared write preconditions, the copy-request validation whose ordering is fixed so the answer does not depend on which end a backend checks first, the copy-source conditions, and the If-Match grammar including weak validators and '*'. multipart.go holds MinPartSize, ValidateMinPartSizes, MultipartPutOptions and the Completion type that makes every backend publish a completed multipart object identically. commit.go holds ErrMutationCommitted and the QuotaStoreProvider capability that lets a wrapper point the runtime at the store whose data the quota counts. staged.go, put_body.go, owned_body.go, owned_reader.go, bytes.go and stream_prepare.go hold the write pipeline: a write is staged, then prepared — the bytes are read or adopted, the digest computed, the metadata cloned, the ETag derived — and only then committed; a body may be an OwnedBody that transfers a buffer exactly once, and an ordinary reader is copied rather than borrowed. metadata.go normalises user metadata and refuses conflicting values for the same normalised key. memory.go and memory_copy.go implement the whole contract in memory behind a single RWMutex, and memory_copy.go captures the source and publishes the destination under that one lock, which is what makes its copy a transaction rather than a read followed by a write.

callers.scope: the S3 HTTP surface — handlePutObject calls s.store.PutObject (:203) and handleListObjectsV2 calls s.store.ListObjectsV2 (:101); the surface treats the contract as the only way to reach bytes
the S3 server holds the contract as its store field and probes its multipart half once at construction (:102), which is why an object-model-only store still serves correctly with a 501 on multipart
the embedded runtime — Instance holds the store, probes its multipart capability at construction (:61), re-derives it after a store swap (:240) and closes it exactly once (:245)
the runtime's guarded-save path, which discovers storage.GuardedWriteStore and refuses the save with ErrGuardedSavesUnsupported when the store does not have it (:143)
the run-through adapter wraps a local storage.Store and a cache storage.Store and presents itself as storage.Store for s3api routing, probing the local store's multipart half at :103
the embedded public library adapts a caller-supplied public store onto the internal contract, adding the optional multipart half only when the caller's store carries it (:120-134)
the CLI composition root — buildStore returns the local store or the run-through adapter (:349 binds it into the runtime), and the result becomes the S3 server's store (:379)
the shared contract suite — withStores runs one property set against the memory, filesystem and workspace backends, and requireMultipart (:82) pins the optional half for the shipped backends

depth_assessment.deletion_test: Deleting the package concentrates the complexity across its callers rather than removing it. The bucket and key rules would have to be restated in every backend; the quoted-MD5 ETag, the composite multipart ETag and the distinction between a one-part and a many-part completion would be reinvented per store; the five checksum digests and the decision to compute or verify a claim would reappear in each backend (which is exactly the drift the package comment at internal/storage/checksum.go:60 records, where workspace verified and memory and filesystem stored the value verbatim); the If-Match grammar and the copy-source conditions would move into the S3 surface and the runtime separately; the three pagination algorithms would diverge per store, so a client would see different truncation from the same data; and the sentinel vocabulary would lose the single upward translation table at internal/s3api/errors.go:127, so refusals would reach clients as unmapped server faults. That is the deep half. The shallow half is the optional-capability mechanism: the interface declares no discovery protocol, so roughly two dozen call sites independently re-derive 'assert the interface, then check its Supports* predicate' (internal/runtime/guarded_save.go:50, internal/runtime/save_requests.go:13, internal/runtime/object_recovery.go:24, internal/runtime/state.go:109, internal/runtime/streams.go:59, internal/s3api/copy.go:85, internal/s3api/request.go:280), and two of those sites even disagree — internal/runtime/save_requests.go:13 checks SupportsDurableSaveRequests before asserting the interface, while internal/runtime/save_requests.go:24 and :71 assert it without re-checking. Deleting that mechanism would not move complexity anywhere; it would concentrate it, but into one place that does not exist yet.

leverage: Callers get one vocabulary for everything they would otherwise re-derive. A bucket name and a key are validated once (internal/storage/util.go:24, :50) and every backend refuses the same inputs. The ETag a client reads back is the same string it may send back on a conditional write, in one format (internal/storage/util.go:76, internal/storage/preconditions.go:80). A checksum claim is either computed by the store or verified by it, never accepted on trust (internal/storage/checksum.go:68). The three pagination algorithms are stated once, so a store truncates identically whatever protocol asks (internal/storage/util.go:192, :220, :273). The multipart completion rules — the 5 MiB minimum and the composite ETag — live in one place (internal/storage/multipart.go:16, internal/storage/util.go:106). The optional interfaces let a caller degrade honestly rather than fail: a store with no storage.ConditionalCopyStore still yields a coherent copy and the interface says so (internal/storage/store.go:86-97), and the runtime refuses a guarded save with a named error rather than performing an unguarded write (internal/runtime/guarded_save.go:143). The shared contract suite makes the promise testable against every backend rather than against one (internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:64).
locality: Change, bugs and knowledge concentrate in internal/storage/*.go: the interface in store.go, the value types in types.go, the validation, ETag and pagination rules in util.go, the digest algorithms and the compute-or-verify decision in checksum.go, the If-Match grammar and copy-source conditions in preconditions.go, the multipart completion rules in multipart.go, the staged-write and owned-payload machinery in staged.go, put_body.go, owned_body.go, owned_reader.go and stream_prepare.go, and the sentinel vocabulary across errors.go, guarded.go, save_requests.go and recovery.go. The root package imports nothing from the rest of the repository, so a rule change lands in one file plus the backends that must honour it. Backend-specific behaviour sits behind the contract in internal/storage/fs, internal/storage/workspace, internal/runthrough, internal/runtime and internal/embedded, and the surfaces that consume it sit in internal/s3api, cmd/stow-s3 and pkg/stow.
risks: The optional-capability discovery protocol is unstated and re-derived at every call site. Around two dozen inline type assertions implement 'assert the interface, then check its Supports* predicate' independently (internal/runtime/guarded_save.go:50, internal/runtime/save_requests.go:13, internal/runtime/object_recovery.go:24, internal/runtime/state.go:109, internal/runtime/streams.go:59, internal/runtime/usage_recovery.go:17, internal/s3api/copy.go:85, internal/s3api/request.go:280), and two sites already disagree about whether the predicate must be checked (internal/runtime/save_requests.go:13 against :24 and :71). A new capability has no home until a caller invents one.

A wrapper store silently erases the capabilities of the store it wraps. runthrough.Adapter forwards storage.MultipartStore (internal/runthrough/multipart_adapter.go:9) and storage.ConditionalCopyStore (internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:227) but implements none of storage.GuardedWriteStore, storage.SaveRequestStore, storage.RecoveryHoldStore, storage.PutChecksumStore, storage.RangeStore, storage.UsageRevisionStore, storage.ObjectUsageStore or storage.StagedWriteStore, and the CLI binds the adapter — not the local store — into the runtime (cmd/stow-s3/main.go:343, cmd/stow-s3/main.go:349). The runtime's probes therefore find nothing in run-through mode: a guarded save is refused with ErrGuardedSavesUnsupported (internal/runtime/guarded_save.go:143) and a durable save request with storage.ErrSaveRequestsUnsupported (internal/runtime/guarded_save.go:140), even though the filesystem store underneath supports both (internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:46, :49).

Four optional capabilities have exactly one adapter and are therefore hypothetical seams. storage.SaveRequestStore is implemented only by fs.FilesystemStore (internal/storage/fs/save_requests.go:26); storage.RecoveryHoldStore only by fs.FilesystemStore (internal/storage/fs/recovery_holds.go:65) — the workspace package's recovery holds are a different model keyed on workspace and checkpoint references (internal/storage/workspace/recovery_holds.go:28) and never call BeginRecoveryHold; storage.UsageRevisionStore only by fs.FilesystemStore (internal/storage/fs/usage_revision.go:5); storage.ObjectUsageStore only by fs.FilesystemStore (internal/storage/fs/fs_list.go:134).

One concrete type carries different capabilities on different operating systems. FilesystemStore.SupportsGuardedWrites() is true only on darwin and linux (internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:46), and SupportsDurableSaveRequests and SupportsRecoveryHolds both defer to it (internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:49, internal/storage/fs/recovery_holds.go:52). The interface says nothing about this, so a caller reasoning from the concrete type is wrong on Windows and the failure is a missing capability rather than a compile error.

Two of the contract's strongest promises live only in prose: CopyObject publishes the destination from exactly one version (internal/storage/store.go:34) and DeleteObjects confirms a key that was not there (internal/storage/store.go:23). The compiler enforces neither, so a new adapter can satisfy the signature and break both; only the shared suite catches it (internal/storage/copy_contract_test.go:35, internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:64).

The object model is S3-shaped in behaviour, not only in names, and the package does not say so: the ETag is a quoted MD5 (internal/storage/util.go:76), a completed multipart object's ETag is the S3 composite '-N' form unless there was exactly one part (internal/storage/util.go:130), the checksum encodings are the S3 base64 wire forms (internal/storage/checksum.go:35), ListObjectsV2 counts common prefixes against MaxKeys (internal/storage/util.go:309), and the bucket-name rules are AWS's reserved-prefix rules (internal/storage/util.go:16). A second protocol inherits S3's semantics whether it wants them or not.

The error vocabulary is the contract's only cross-layer contract and it is wider than the core interface produces. ErrObjectUncertain, ErrSaveConflict, ErrSaveRequestUnknown, ErrRecoveryHeld and the capability refusals are declared in internal/storage/errors.go, internal/storage/guarded.go, internal/storage/save_requests.go and internal/storage/recovery.go, and the S3 surface translates them in one table (internal/s3api/errors.go:127). A new store that invents its own refusal instead of returning a sentinel reaches the client as a 500 rather than the mapped S3 code.

priority.rationale: The blast radius is the whole system: nine concrete implementations and every surface (S3 HTTP, embedded runtime, run-through adapter, embedded public library, CLI, and the WASM bridge through embedded.storeAdapter) bind to this one interface, so a change to the core twelve methods or to the shared value rules moves all of them. The unclear seam is the optional-capability mechanism, which is declared nowhere and re-derived at roughly two dozen sites, and the hidden coupling is demonstrated: the run-through adapter drops eight of the optional capabilities the filesystem store has, so run-through mode silently loses guarded saves, durable save requests and recovery holds, and the filesystem backend drops three of them on Windows (internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:46). This is not P0 because nothing is currently broken in the common path and the core contract is well covered by a shared property suite run against three backends (internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:64); it is P1 because the degradation is silent, the affected features are the durability and recovery ones, and the discovery protocol has no single place to be fixed.

next_action: State the capability-discovery protocol once, in internal/storage, and route every call site through it: add a single probe (for example a Capabilities struct returned by one helper such as storage.CapabilitiesOf(store)) that performs the type assertions and the Supports* predicates together, then replace the inline assertions in internal/runtime/guarded_save.go:50, internal/runtime/save_requests.go:13, internal/runtime/object_recovery.go:24, internal/runtime/state.go:109, internal/runtime/streams.go:59, internal/runtime/usage_recovery.go:17, internal/s3api/copy.go:85 and internal/s3api/request.go:280 with it. Separately, make runthrough.Adapter forward the optional capabilities of the store it wraps (GuardedWriteStore, SaveRequestStore, RecoveryHoldStore, PutChecksumStore) instead of dropping them, so the runtime's probes find the capabilities the local store actually has (internal/runthrough/adapter.go:39-41, cmd/stow-s3/main.go:349). The interface that should change is the optional-capability half of internal/storage/store.go and a new discovery helper beside it — not the core twelve methods, which are correct and well tested.

title: The storage.Store seam: one object-model contract, nine production implementations, three selection sites
summary: internal/storage/store.go:13 declares storage.Store, the object model every backend in this repository satisfies - buckets, objects, versions, preconditions, copy, listing and close - and nothing else; the file's own comment at :9-12 says multipart is deliberately not a member. Nine production types sit behind it: three backing stores that own the bytes (storage.MemoryStore at internal/storage/memory.go:41, fs.FilesystemStore at internal/storage/fs/fs.go:24, workspace.Store at internal/storage/workspace/workspace.go:14), three adapters that wrap another store (runthrough.Adapter at internal/runthrough/adapter.go:28, runtime.StoreAdapter at internal/runtime/adapter.go:15, embedded.storeAdapter at internal/embedded/store.go:105), and three decorators that embed the interface (embedded.storeWithMultipart at internal/embedded/store.go:112, embedded.storeWithStaging at internal/embedded/staged.go:19, cmd/stow-s3.runThroughRuntimeStore at cmd/stow-s3/runtime_store.go:61). Selection happens in three places, not one: the native CLI (parseBackend at cmd/stow-s3/main.go:99, openLocalStore at :117, buildStore at cmd/stow-s3/store.go:24, bindNativeRuntimeStore at cmd/stow-s3/runtime_store.go:37), the Go library (pkg/stow.OpenFilesystem at pkg/stow/filesystem_native.go:14, pkg/stow.OpenWorkspace at pkg/stow/workspace.go:116, pkg/stow.Open at pkg/stow/runtime.go:9), and the WASM bridge (openHostRuntime at cmd/stow-wasm/host_store_js.go:37, whose hostStore implements the public embedded.Store and reaches the seam only by being adapted at internal/embedded/store.go:120). What genuinely varies across the seam is durability, on-disk layout, which optional capability interfaces the store satisfies, the cost of a quota scan, and whether a reset exists; what deliberately does not vary is the object model, the precondition semantics, the copy-atomicity contract, and the error sentinel vocabulary.

trace.scope: the --backend flag is declared, defaulting to "filesystem"; this string is the only thing that selects a backend
parseBackend turns the flag into a typed runtime.Backend and refuses workspace and unknown values
openLocalStore maps the typed backend to fs.NewFilesystemStore or storage.NewMemoryStore
buildStore decides whether the local store is served directly or wrapped in a runthrough.Adapter with a cache store and an outbox
bindNativeRuntimeStore wraps whatever was built in a runtime.StoreAdapter, so quota and authority are enforced above the seam
the selected backend writes the object: atomicfile.WriteStream into <dataDir>/buckets/<bucket>/objects/<key>

evidence.detail: storage.Store declares the object model in 12 methods and nothing else; the doc comment at :9-12 states that multipart is deliberately not a member because it is how one protocol happens to stream an object larger than memory.
var _ storage.Store = (*FilesystemStore)(nil) - the filesystem backend's compile-time assertion that it satisfies the seam.
var _ storage.Store = (*Store)(nil) - the workspace backend's compile-time assertion.
var _ storage.Store = (*StoreAdapter)(nil) - the runtime compatibility adapter's compile-time assertion.
var _ storage.Store = (*storeAdapter)(nil) - the public-to-internal adapter's compile-time assertion.
var _ storage.Store = (*runThroughRuntimeStore)(nil) - the CLI's run-through wrapper's compile-time assertion.

buildStore returns *runthrough.Adapter in a storage.Store return position; this return statement is the compile-time proof that runthrough.Adapter satisfies the seam, because internal/runthrough carries no explicit var _ assertion.

MemoryStore.PutObject is the only in-package implementation of the full method set, so it needs no var _ assertion; internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:28 returns storage.NewMemoryStore() in a storage.Store position, which is the construction-site proof.

withStores runs one contract suite over the three backing stores (memory at :26, filesystem at :33, workspace at :49); the test file imports the concrete backends it asserts on, which is the only back-edge in the Go packages.

hostStore is not an adapter of storage.Store: its ListBuckets at :178 returns []stow.Bucket and its PutObject at cmd/stow-wasm/host_store_io_js.go:21 takes []byte, so it satisfies the public embedded.Store (internal/embedded/store.go:15) and reaches the internal seam only via embedded.adaptStore at internal/embedded/store.go:120.

The sentinel vocabulary every implementation must return: ErrBucketNotFound, ErrInvalidBucketName, ErrBucketExists, ErrObjectNotFound, ErrInvalidKey, ErrInvalidUpload, ErrInvalidPart, ErrObjectUncertain, ErrEntityTooSmall, ErrUploadNotFound, ErrNoSuchUpload, ErrPreconditionFailed, ErrChecksumMismatch, ErrMD5Mismatch, ErrBucketNotEmpty, ErrMultipartUnsupported.
translate maps the public embedded sentinels onto the internal ones, so a caller-supplied store cannot change the error vocabulary underneath the run-through adapter.
CheckWritePreconditions is shared by every backend, so the meaning of IfMatch and IfNoneMatch does not vary across the seam.
The filesystem sink: atomicfile.WriteStream writes the record into <dataDir>/buckets/<bucket>/objects/<key> (path built at internal/storage/fs/fs.go:134).

The seam's optional capabilities change observable behaviour above it: a store that implements storage.ObjectUsageStore is scanned once per bucket, one that does not is walked with paginated ListObjectsV2 calls (the fallback at :121-140).

interface.types: storage.Store is a 12-method interface: CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, HeadBucket, ListBuckets, PutObject, GetObject, HeadObject, DeleteObject, DeleteObjects, CopyObject, ListObjectsV2, Close. Objects are addressed as a (bucket, key) pair; a write carries storage.PutOptions (ContentType, Metadata, ChecksumAlgorithm, ChecksumValue, IfMatch, IfNoneMatch, ComputeChecksum, and internally Guard and RequestKey, internal/storage/types.go:28); a read returns an io.ReadCloser plus a *storage.ObjectMeta; a listing takes storage.ListOptions (Prefix, Delimiter, ContinuationToken, MaxKeys, StartAfter) and returns a *storage.ListResult. The interface also declares five optional capability interfaces in the same file - MultipartStore (:48), ConditionalCopyStore (:98), UsageRevisionStore (:104), PutChecksumStore (:109), ObjectUsageStore (:116) - plus SaveRequestStore (internal/storage/save_requests.go:24), RecoveryHoldStore (internal/storage/recovery.go:29) and GuardedWriteStore (internal/storage/guarded.go:12) in sibling files. A substituter must also honour the shared helpers the package exports for it - storage.ValidateBucketName, storage.ValidateKey, storage.CheckWritePreconditions, storage.ValidateCopyRequest, storage.CheckCopySourceConditions, storage.PreparePut, storage.NewRecordVersion, storage.NewUploadID - because the interface's own doc comment relies on those rules; the interface itself states only the method set.
invariants: Every method validates the bucket name and the key with the shared helpers before touching state, and a missing bucket is refused as storage.ErrBucketNotFound and a missing key as storage.ErrObjectNotFound (internal/storage/memory.go:138-149, internal/storage/fs/fs.go:305-324, internal/storage/workspace/objects.go:24-29).

A missing bucket is refused before the request body is read; internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:102 asserts the body is not touched, because the memory backend read and hashed it under the store lock.
Write preconditions are evaluated by the shared storage.CheckWritePreconditions (internal/storage/preconditions.go:11), so IfMatch and IfNoneMatch mean the same thing in every backend.

CopyObject publishes the destination from exactly one version of the source (internal/storage/store.go:34-36); a store that cannot do that atomically says so by not implementing storage.ConditionalCopyStore.
DeleteObjects confirms a key that was not present as deleted and returns the confirmed keys in request order (internal/storage/store.go:23-33, internal/storage/memory.go:289-295).
A returned *ObjectMeta is a copy: metadata maps are cloned so a caller cannot mutate stored state through it (internal/storage/memory.go:19-22, internal/storage/util.go:147).

Close is idempotent for the filesystem and workspace stores (internal/storage/fs/fs.go:441-450, internal/storage/workspace/workspace.go:201-218); the memory store's Close is a no-op (internal/storage/memory.go:451-453).
error_modes: storage.ErrBucketNotFound, ErrBucketExists, ErrBucketNotEmpty, ErrObjectNotFound, ErrInvalidBucketName, ErrInvalidKey, ErrPreconditionFailed, ErrInvalidPart, ErrEntityTooSmall, ErrUploadNotFound, ErrNoSuchUpload, ErrChecksumMismatch, ErrMultipartUnsupported, ErrObjectUncertain (internal/storage/errors.go:5-30). A substituter must return these sentinels rather than its own errors.
storage.ErrMutationCommitted means the write landed and a later step failed; it wraps a cause and must reach the caller intact (internal/embedded/store.go:146-151, internal/s3api/errors.go:181).
storage.ErrSaveConflict for a guarded write whose observation no longer holds (internal/storage/guarded.go:9, :30-40).

storage.ErrSaveRequestUnsupported-family errors: ErrSaveRequestsUnsupported, ErrInvalidSaveRequest, ErrSaveRequestConflict, ErrSaveRequestNotFound, ErrSaveRequestNotCommitted, ErrSaveRequestUnknown, ErrSaveRequestFull (internal/storage/save_requests.go:8-16).
storage.ErrRecoveryHoldsUnsupported, ErrInvalidRecoveryHold, ErrRecoveryHoldNotFound, ErrRecoveryHoldFull, ErrRecoveryHeld (internal/storage/recovery.go:8-17).
The S3 layer maps the sentinels to S3 error codes in one table (internal/s3api/errors.go:127-145); a store that invents its own error becomes a 500 internal storage error rather than the right code.
ordering: CopyObjectCond's source conditions are evaluated against the version the store copies, under the same lock that publishes the destination (internal/storage/memory_copy.go:20-31, internal/storage/fs/fs_copy.go:24, internal/storage/workspace/objects.go:220-222).

The multipart interface is whole rather than write-only because a consumer that reconciles in-flight uploads at open must be able to ask what is in flight (internal/storage/store.go:42-47); the runtime skips that reconciliation for a store that does not implement MultipartStore (internal/runtime/state.go:94-106).

A part carries the ETag the completing call identifies it by (internal/storage/types.go:142-148), and completion part numbers must be strictly ascending with no duplicates (internal/storage/util.go:106).
In the CLI the store is built before the runtime wrapper is applied (cmd/stow-s3/main.go:343 then cmd/stow-s3/main.go:349), so the authority is resolved before the run-through adapter is constructed.
A store's own writes are the only thing that settles its save journal: fs.settleSaveLocked is called at the head of every mutating path (internal/storage/fs/fs.go:220, :237, :368, :395).
configuration: A substituter is chosen by construction, not by configuration inside the interface: the CLI switches on runtime.Backend (cmd/stow-s3/main.go:117), the library exposes one constructor per backend (pkg/stow/filesystem_native.go:14, pkg/stow/workspace.go:116), and the embedded path takes a caller-supplied store (internal/embedded/runtime.go:32-44).

The optional capability interfaces are discovered by type assertion at the point of use, never declared: storage.MultipartStore (internal/runtime/instance.go:61, internal/s3api/server.go:102), storage.ConditionalCopyStore (internal/runtime/objects.go:320), storage.ObjectUsageStore (internal/runtime/state.go:109), storage.SaveRequestStore (internal/runtime/save_requests.go:13), storage.RecoveryHoldStore (internal/runtime/object_recovery.go:24), storage.GuardedWriteStore (internal/runtime/guarded_save.go:50), storage.PutChecksumStore (internal/runtime/adapter.go:255, internal/s3api/request.go:280).
Quota options (MaxBytes, MaxObjects, MaxMultipartUploads) are applied by the runtime above the seam, not by the store (internal/runtime/types.go:106-133).

The filesystem backend takes an exclusive directory lock and refuses to open a directory another process holds (internal/storage/fs/fs.go:66-70), and its guarded-write and durable-save-request support is platform-conditional (internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:46-49).

The CLI's run-through mode adds a second store - a cache store under <data-dir>/cache - and an outbox file, so the cache is a second instance of the same seam rather than a different kind of store (cmd/stow-s3/store.go:30, cmd/stow-s3/main.go:334-337).

implementation: internal/storage/store.go holds the interface and the value types that cross it, and no behaviour of its own: the 12-method Store, the optional MultipartStore, ConditionalCopyStore, UsageRevisionStore, PutChecksumStore and ObjectUsageStore, plus CopyOptions and CopyRequest. The behaviour lives in the package's siblings - the shared validators and helpers in internal/storage/util.go, internal/storage/preconditions.go, internal/storage/stream_prepare.go and internal/storage/checksum.go; the sentinel vocabulary in internal/storage/errors.go; the guard fingerprint in internal/storage/guarded.go; and the three backing stores in internal/storage/memory.go, internal/storage/fs/ and internal/storage/workspace/. The three adapters that bridge the seam to the layers above it each carry their own decisions: runthrough.Adapter decides whether a write reaches the upstream, journals it in an outbox and falls back to a weaker copy when the local store cannot evaluate source conditions (internal/runthrough/adapter.go:26-121, internal/runthrough/mutations_adapter.go:227-290); runtime.StoreAdapter routes every verb through a runtime.Instance so quotas, authority and usage accounting stay in one place (internal/runtime/adapter.go:12-27); embedded.storeAdapter translates the public embedded contract into the internal one, carries the optional halves only when the caller's store does, and expresses DeleteObjects and CopyObject through the primitives rather than refusing them (internal/embedded/store.go:103-134, :273-308).

callers.scope: openLocalStore is the CLI's selection switch: it maps a runtime.Backend to fs.NewFilesystemStore or storage.NewMemoryStore and log.Fatal's on anything else.

buildStore is the CLI's composition site: local mode returns the plain store and a nil adapter without ever constructing an upstream client; run-through mode wraps it in a runthrough.Adapter with a cache store and a file outbox.

bindNativeRuntimeStore is the CLI's enforcement site: every store the server serves is wrapped in runtime.StoreAdapter, and in run-through mode in runThroughRuntimeStore, so the runtime owns quota and authority.

pkg/stow.OpenFilesystem opens one exclusively locked durable directory and hands the store to runtime.OpenWithStore; on a platform that is not linux or darwin the constructor returns ErrUnsupportedBackend instead (pkg/stow/filesystem_unsupported.go:5).
pkg/stow.OpenWorkspace opens a workspace store and hands it to runtime.OpenWithStore with BackendWorkspace, then claims an advisory session lock on the directory.
pkg/stow.Open is the library's general entry point; with no store it opens memory only, because internal/runtime/types.go:88 refuses any backend but memory when no store is bound.
openHostRuntime is the WASM bridge's construction site: it hands the JS-host-backed store to embedded.Open as Options.Store, with BackendHost.

s3api.New takes a storage.Store and is the seam's largest consumer; it discovers the optional MultipartStore by assertion at :102 and its handlers call the store directly (internal/s3api/handlers_bucket.go:203, :222).
runtime.OpenWithStore binds a storage.Store into an Instance, which is the layer that turns a store into a quota-enforcing, authority-checked environment and the only place that resets it.
withStores is the seam's own test caller: one contract suite is run over memory, filesystem and workspace.

depth_assessment.deletion_test: Delete the storage.Store interface and the complexity does not vanish - it concentrates. The object model, the precondition rules (internal/storage/preconditions.go), the copy-atomicity rule (internal/storage/store.go:34-36), the delete-idempotency rule (:23-33) and the sentinel vocabulary (internal/storage/errors.go) would each have to be restated inside all nine implementations and inside internal/runtime, internal/s3api, internal/embedded and internal/runthrough, and those restatements would then have to agree with one another. The interface is the one place those rules are written down. Deleting the declaring file alone (internal/storage/store.go) would move the type declarations and nothing else, because the shared rules live in the sibling files of the same package - the depth is in the contract the file names, not in the file.

leverage: Callers get one object model with one error vocabulary and one set of precondition and copy-atomicity rules, whatever is underneath. internal/s3api writes one error table against storage sentinels (internal/s3api/errors.go:127-145) and does not need to know which backend it is serving; internal/runtime enforces quota and authority once, above the seam, because it owns the store rather than reimplementing it; the contract suite at internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:64 runs one set of assertions over memory, filesystem and workspace, so a new backend is checked by construction rather than by a new test file; and the embedded path lets an outside caller supply a store at all without importing internal (internal/embedded/store.go:103-134).
locality: Change, bugs and knowledge about the object model concentrate in internal/storage: the interface and the shared helpers in internal/storage/preconditions.go, internal/storage/util.go and internal/storage/stream_prepare.go, and the sentinel list in internal/storage/errors.go. Backend-specific behaviour concentrates in internal/storage/fs/, internal/storage/workspace/ and internal/storage/memory.go. The selection rules concentrate in three places rather than one - cmd/stow-s3/main.go:99 and :117, cmd/stow-s3/store.go:24, and the three pkg/stow constructors - so a change to 'which backend is legal where' has to be made in the CLI and in the library separately.
risks: The optional capability interfaces are discovered by type assertion at the point of use, so a caller's behaviour depends on which backend the selection switch chose and the coupling is invisible in the type system: internal/runtime/state.go:109 switches between one quota scan and a paginated rescan, internal/runtime/save_requests.go:13 decides whether a lost write can be replayed, internal/runtime/object_recovery.go:24 decides whether recovery holds exist at all, and internal/s3api/request.go:280 decides whether the server computes a put checksum.

storage.SaveRequestStore (internal/storage/save_requests.go:24) and storage.RecoveryHoldStore (internal/storage/recovery.go:29) have one production adapter each - fs.FilesystemStore - so they read as substitutable but are not; a second backend would silently lose durable save requests and recovery holds rather than fail to compile.

The embedded path is the one adapter that does not carry the conditional-copy guarantee: embedded.storeAdapter.CopyObject (internal/embedded/store.go:291-308) does get-then-put, so a caller-supplied store silently gets the weaker guarantee the interface documents at internal/storage/store.go:90-97.
The CLI refuses --backend workspace (cmd/stow-s3/main.go:103-108) while the library supports it, so the same word names two different capabilities depending on the surface.

The filesystem backend's guarded-write and durable-save-request support is platform-conditional (internal/storage/fs/save_journal.go:46-49 returns true only on darwin and linux), so the same backend silently loses those capabilities on another platform.
Selection is spread over three surfaces with three separate switch statements, so a policy that makes a backend illegal in one place can be bypassed in another.

priority.rationale: The blast radius is the widest in the repository: storage.Store sits under the S3 server, the embedded runtime, the WASM bridge, the run-through adapter and the MCP object host, and a change to it moves nine implementations plus internal/runtime, internal/s3api and internal/embedded. The risk is not the interface's shape but the type-assertion discovery of the optional capability interfaces, which couples the selection switch at cmd/stow-s3/main.go:99 to runtime behaviour in internal/runtime that no type records. It is not P0 because the contract suite at internal/storage/backend_contract_test.go:64 pins the three backing stores to one set of assertions and the sentinel vocabulary is centralised in internal/storage/errors.go, so a divergence shows up as a failing contract rather than as silent data loss.

next_action: Document the seam as a contract page next to the environment implementation document referenced at cmd/stow-s3/main.go:106, stating: the nine production implementations and the three selection sites; the optional capability interfaces with their true adapter counts, naming storage.SaveRequestStore and storage.RecoveryHoldStore as one-adapter interfaces that are not substitution points; and the discovery-by-assertion rule, including the consequence that storage.ObjectUsageStore changes the cost of a quota scan. The concrete interface that should change is the one in internal/storage/store.go: give each optional interface a doc comment stating its adapter count and the discovery rule, and either give storage.SaveRequestStore and storage.RecoveryHoldStore a second adapter or stop declaring them as interfaces so the type system stops advertising a substitution that cannot happen.

title: Python client package (stow_s3)
summary: stow_s3 is the Python client package for the stow local S3 service. It starts a native `stow-s3 serve` child process, reads the endpoint and generated credentials from a versioned JSON readiness record over an inherited pipe descriptor, and hands the caller a Session that owns that child. It also resolves the native binary, wraps the `stow-s3 workspace` CLI as synchronous JSON helpers, and owns a `workspace serve` child for a persistent workspace. It is a second, hand-maintained implementation of the same contract the TypeScript client in packages/stow-s3 speaks to the same Go server; it performs no S3 I/O itself and boto3 is an optional extra.

trace.scope: from stow_s3 import with_session - a recipe entry into the session lifecycle
with_session calls open_session and closes the Session in a finally
open_session allocates the readiness pipe (os.pipe) and marks the write end inheritable
subprocess.Popen starts the serve child with build_child_env() and pass_fds=(write_fd,)
the first line read from the readiness descriptor is decoded by parse_ready_message into StowReady
the frozen Session is constructed from the ready record and returned by open_session

evidence.detail: __all__ enumerates the 40-name public surface re-exported from five modules (workspace_serve, bin, ready, session, workspace).
_server_args is the only place the serve argv is built.
build_child_env strips STOW_/S3_/AWS_ and setdefaults GOGC, unconditionally.
parse_ready_message is the strict client half of the readiness protocol.
the Go Message struct is the server half; its Capabilities carries maxMultipartUploads (ready.go:36), which neither client reads.
the TypeScript client pins READY_FD=3, while Python allocates a dynamic pipe fd (session.py:313).
the only cross-client drift gate covers SESSION_GOGC and the ownership marker (check-version.mjs:173-198), not the ready message or the serve argv.
_run_workspace_command shells out to the resolved binary as [workspace, ...args] without a shell and raises on a nonzero exit; run_workspace_command decodes one JSON object from stdout.

interface.types: A frozen Session dataclass (endpoint, access_key_id, secret_access_key, region, data_dir, max_bytes, max_objects, mode, backend, binary_version, protocol_version, capabilities, owns_data_dir, plus private process/log/closed fields) whose s3_client(**kwargs) lazily builds a boto3 client; module functions open_session/with_session, parse_ready_message returning StowReady/StowCapabilities, binary helpers resolve_stow_binary(_detailed)/require_stow_binary/stow_binary_available/describe_source returning ResolvedBinary, and 16 synchronous workspace veneer functions returning WorkspaceJSON.
invariants: open_session validates limits before spawning and returns a Session only after a complete readiness record is parsed (session.py:298-380).
close() is idempotent, suppresses errors on the way out, stops the child (SIGTERM then SIGKILL), and removes only a data directory the session itself created (session.py:166-189).
The child is spawned with an explicit env whose STOW_/S3_/AWS_-prefixed entries are removed; GOGC defaults to 50 unless the caller set it (session.py:61-70).

parse_ready_message rejects any protocolVersion other than 1, a non-object payload, and any missing or wrongly-typed required field; maxConcurrentRequests is optional and defaults to 0, and a reported 0 limit is carried through rather than treated as missing (ready.py:103-149).
A supplied data_dir selects the filesystem backend and is preserved on close; a session-created temporary data_dir selects the memory backend and is removed (session.py:184,306-320).
error_modes: StowBinaryNotFoundError when no executable binary resolves (bin.py:118-123).
StowProtocolError with code protocol_mismatch or internal on a bad ready record, an exited child, or a non-object payload (ready.py:25-35, session.py:246-250).
TimeoutError when readiness does not arrive within STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=15 (session.py:237-242).
ValueError for negative max_bytes/max_objects or a non-positive max_request_bytes/max_concurrent_requests (session.py:298-303).
WorkspaceCommandError, carrying command/returncode/stderr, on a nonzero `workspace` CLI exit (workspace.py:15-23); ImportError from s3_client when boto3 is absent (session.py:148-156).
ordering: The parent closes its copy of the readiness write end only after Popen, so the reader sees EOF if the child dies before writing (session.py:354-358).
with_session closes the Session in a finally block, so cleanup runs even when the caller's block raises (session.py:407-420).
The readiness line is read on a daemon thread joined with a timeout; the descriptor is closed exactly once by that reader (session.py:208-251).
configuration: STOW_BIN overrides the binary path, after the bundled platform wheel and before the monorepo and PATH fallbacks (bin.py:89-103).
_ISOLATED_ENV_PREFIXES = ('STOW_','S3_','AWS_') are stripped; GOGC is the only GO variable the client sets (session.py:50,58,67).
max_bytes/max_objects default to 16 MiB and 1000; max_request_bytes and max_concurrent_requests are opt-in and passed through to serve (session.py:33-34,277-284,322-325).
boto3 is an optional dependency imported lazily inside s3_client (pyproject.toml:28-29, session.py:148-156).

implementation: session.py owns the child-process lifecycle: _server_args assembles the serve argv (session.py:254-274), open_session allocates the readiness pipe, resolves the binary, validates limits, spawns the child with build_child_env() and pass_fds, then reads and parses the ready line and constructs the Session (session.py:277-389); close()/_stop_process own shutdown (session.py:166-205). ready.py owns strict decoding of the versioned message into StowReady/StowCapabilities (ready.py:38-149). bin.py owns the four-rule resolution precedence and the ResolvedBinary source tag (bin.py:89-123). workspace.py is a thin synchronous veneer over the `stow-s3 workspace` CLI that builds argv, checks the exit status and decodes JSON (workspace.py:26-322). workspace_serve.py owns a `workspace serve` child and parses its separate readiness record (workspace_serve.py:38-98). The package duplicates the TypeScript client's contract by hand: both strip STOW_/S3_/AWS_ (session.py:50 vs start.ts:191), both default GOGC to 50 (session.py:58 vs start.ts:22), both resolve bundled-then-env-then-monorepo-then-PATH (bin.py:89-103 vs bin.ts:131-148), and both require the same seven string fields (binaryVersion, endpoint, region, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, mode, backend) plus a capabilities object. They diverge on: fd allocation (dynamic pipe fd vs READY_FD=3, session.py:313 vs ready-reader.ts:63); legacy fallback (Python has none; TypeScript parses the legacy STOW_READY stdout line, ready-reader.ts:255-276); env-stripping scope (Python always strips, TypeScript only when isolatedEnvironment, start.ts:185); access-key injection (TypeScript sets STOW_LOCAL_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET, start.ts:208-213; Python has no equivalent); argv ordering and content (Python hardcodes --port 0, --host 127.0.0.1, --mode local and appends the transport limits after --parent-pid, session.py:254-274,322-325; TypeScript orders port/data-dir/host first, places transport limits earlier and supports --base-host, --region and the cache flags, start.ts:134-180); and zero-limit policy (Python accepts 0 at session.py:298 while the TypeScript session rejects 0 at session.ts:94-102).

callers.scope: imports with_session and opens a session around a conditional-write recipe
imports with_session and opens a session over a caller-named data directory
imports with_session for the smallest end-to-end recipe
imports with_session to stage inputs and outputs through a session
release smoke: imports __version__, with_session, prepare_workspace and serve_workspace
the lifecycle/protocol test suite for open_session/with_session/build_child_env
the parser suite for parse_ready_message
exercises the workspace veneer and WorkspaceCommandError
exercises open_session when the child cannot be spawned
the binary-resolution suite for resolve_stow_binary_detailed/require_stow_binary

depth_assessment.deletion_test: Deleting packages/stow-s3-py removes the only Python binding. No in-repo Go or TypeScript component imports it, so its internal complexity does not reappear in another module of this repository; its callers are four example recipes, a release smoke script and its own test suite, all of which would have to be deleted or rewritten. session.py, ready.py and bin.py each own decisions a replacement would have to re-implement (process lifetime, strict wire parsing, resolution precedence), so the package is not a pass-through; workspace.py is a thin veneer over the native CLI and __init__.py is a re-export barrel, which is why the depth is mixed rather than deep.

leverage: Callers get a one-line disposable S3 endpoint (with_session), strict failure against an incompatible server, an actionable missing-binary error, and synchronous JSON workspace helpers, without re-implementing child lifecycle, readiness parsing, environment isolation, binary precedence, or the workspace CLI argument grammar.
locality: Change concentrates in session.py (lifecycle, argv, env) and ready.py (wire protocol). Knowledge is split across four parsers of the same protocol (internal/ready/ready.go, packages/stow-s3/src/ready.ts, the legacy branch in ready-reader.ts, and ready.py) and only SESSION_GOGC and the ownership marker are drift-gated by scripts/check-version.mjs.
risks: The ready protocol is implemented independently here and in packages/stow-s3, and scripts/check-version.mjs gates only SESSION_GOGC and the ownership marker (check-version.mjs:173-198), so READY_PROTOCOL_VERSION, the capability field set and the serve argv can drift with no failing check.

Python insists on the versioned fd record and has no legacy STOW_READY fallback, unlike the TypeScript reader (ready-reader.ts:255-276), so a server that ignores --ready-fd starts the child and then fails the session (session.py:245-250).
The readiness descriptor is a dynamically allocated pipe fd in Python (session.py:313) and a fixed fd 3 in TypeScript (ready-reader.ts:63); both document one protocol but not one fd contract.

build_child_env strips STOW_/S3_/AWS_ unconditionally (session.py:61-70) and is used by workspace_serve (workspace_serve.py:69), while TypeScript strips only when isolatedEnvironment is set (start.ts:185) and workspace-serve.ts spawns with no env override (workspace-serve.ts:35); the same `workspace serve` child therefore gets a different environment per client.
