Python's serve argv hardcodes --port 0, --host 127.0.0.1 and --mode local and appends --max-concurrent-requests/--max-request-bytes after --parent-pid (session.py:254-274,322-325), so it cannot express the region, base-host or cache options the TypeScript argv can (start.ts:134-180).
Python accepts max_bytes/max_objects of 0 as 'no limit' (session.py:298) whereas the TypeScript session rejects 0 (session.ts:94-102), so the two clients disagree on a value the caller can pass.

priority.rationale: Two hand-maintained clients speak one protocol to one Go server, and the drift gate covers only GOGC and the ownership marker, so a change to the ready message or the serve argv can break the Python client with no failing check. Blast radius is the stow-s3 Python client package, its example recipes and the consumer smoke script, not the Go request path, which keeps impact at P2.

next_action: Write the ready-message and serve-argv contract down once (e.g. docs/session-protocol.md, generated from internal/ready/ready.go) and extend scripts/check-version.mjs to gate READY_PROTOCOL_VERSION and the required capability field names against both packages/stow-s3/src/ready.ts and packages/stow-s3-py/src/stow_s3/ready.py. The concrete interfaces to change are parse_ready_message / parseReadyMessage (ready.py:103, ready.ts:82) and _server_args / buildServeArgs (session.py:254, start.ts:128).

title: TypeScript client package (@chester-hill-solutions/stow-s3)
summary: packages/stow-s3 is the published TypeScript client for stow. Its Node core owns the child-process lifecycle: it resolves the native stow-s3 binary, spawns `serve` with an argv and a child environment it builds, waits for one JSON readiness record written to inherited descriptor 3, and returns an AWS SDK v3 S3Client bound to the loopback endpoint and generated credentials. It also exposes an embedded in-process facade over a Go WASM host (synchronous EmbeddedStow and the asynchronous worker/browser variants), workspace verbs that shell the native `workspace` subcommands, an ownership-guarded data-directory reset, upstream credential resolution from the environment, and a doctor diagnostic. Its callers are the repository's runnable example recipes, the documentation site's example-checking test, its own test suite, the npm-consumer smoke script, and (outside the repository) any npm consumer. This unit maps the package's export surface and its Node client core; the browser content-store, project library, browser persistence and embedded-host-bridge internals are carried by separate coverage units.

trace.scope: withStow(fn) is the caller's entry into the package; the callback receives {s3, bucket}
openStow validates limits, picks a data dir, and calls startStowWithReady with isolatedEnvironment and parentPid
startStowWithReady builds the serve argv and child environment, resolves the binary, and spawns it
spawn passes stdio ["ignore","pipe","pipe","pipe"] so the fourth entry is the readiness descriptor
waitForReady accumulates descriptor 3 until a newline-terminated record, with a legacy stdout STOW_READY fallback
parseReadyMessage strictly validates the protocol version and every required field
createStowInstance turns the parsed endpoint/credentials/region into an AWS SDK client factory and lifecycle helpers
createStowS3Client yields the S3Client whose send() carries the endpoint and credentials as a signed HTTP request to the loopback stow server

evidence.detail: The export map publishes ".", "./embedded", "./node-wasm", "./workspace", "./browser", "./browser-s3", "./worker", "./browser-wasm" and "./project"; the bin field publishes stow-doctor (package.json:46-48); the only runtime dependencies are @aws-sdk/client-s3, @smithy/signature-v4 and @smithy/types (package.json:68-72).

index.ts is not a pure barrel: it exports the default Stow aggregator with start/connect/awsSdkV3Config/upstream.fromEnv (index.ts:106-148) plus named re-exports, and it deliberately excludes the browser profile (index.ts:19-22).

Only twelve workspace verbs are re-exported at the root; workspace.ts also defines listWorkspaces (workspace.ts:113), adoptWorkspaceHandoff (workspace.ts:190), createWorkspaceDelta (workspace.ts:197) and applyWorkspaceDelta (workspace.ts:204), which are reachable only through the "./workspace" subpath.

The serve argv is [serve --port --data-dir --host] plus optional flags and always --ready-fd <READY_FD>, optionally --parent-pid (start.ts:135-179). There is no --read-only flag, in this argv or in the Python _server_args.

buildChildEnv copies process.env, deletes every key matching /^(STOW_|S3_|AWS_)/ only when isolatedEnvironment is set (start.ts:190-194), defaults GOGC to SESSION_GOGC="50" only when unset and isolated (start.ts:204-206), and sets STOW_LOCAL_ACCESS_KEY_ID/STOW_LOCAL_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY from options.accessKey/secretKey (start.ts:208-213).

READY_FD is pinned to 3 (index 3 is the fourth stdio entry), and the reader only accepts a record terminated by a newline, carrying the unterminated tail forward (ready-reader.ts:190-205; ready-framing.ts:30-34).

parseReadyMessage rejects an unknown protocolVersion (READY_PROTOCOL_VERSION=1, ready.ts:7,96), a non-object payload, and any missing required field, all as StowProtocolError with code protocol_mismatch (ready.ts:38-48).

buildAwsSdkV3Config resolves a credential provider over static credentials, throws StowCredentialsError when neither is supplied (instance.ts:33-62), defaults region to us-east-1 (instance.ts:22,66) and forcePathStyle to true (instance.ts:68).
createStowS3Client adds a build-step middleware that sets x-amz-content-sha256 to UNSIGNED_PAYLOAD, which is what stow's SigV4 verifier accepts (s3-client.ts:8-34).

Session.handoff returns a fresh object with exactly AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL and STOW_BUCKET, and never mutates the parent environment; test/session.test.ts:159-180 pins the key set.

Session.close runs client destroy, instance stop and (only for a self-created data dir) rm as isolated steps and reports all failures, throwing AggregateError when more than one step fails; close is idempotent and later method use throws code "closed", while the dataDir getter (session.ts:223-225) and the s3 field stay readable (session.ts:277-319).

resetOwnedData refuses a directory that is the home directory or an ancestor of the working directory (ownership.ts:49-64) and refuses a directory without the .stow-owner marker; an absent directory is not an error.

resolveStowBinaryDetailed prefers the npm platform package over STOW_BIN, then a monorepo bin/stow-s3, then stow-s3 on PATH (bin.ts:131-148); the platform package outranking STOW_BIN is stated deliberately (bin.ts:122-129). The STOW_BIN path is returned without an executability test; stowBinaryAvailable is what rejects a non-executable resolved path (bin.ts:154-160).

EmbeddedStow is the synchronous in-process facade: every verb is a JSON request through EmbeddedHost.call, escalated to the binary protocol (EMBEDDED_BINARY_PROTOCOL_VERSION=2) when the host provides callBinary (embedded.ts:1-2,126-137,248-282), with responses validated in decodeEmbeddedResponse (embedded.ts:284-316).

loadNodeWasmHost loads wasm_exec.js into the current realm, instantiates ./stow-runtime.wasm, waits for globalThis.stow and exposes call/callBinary/callBinaryAsync/openHost/close over the Go WASM runtime; close drains the runtime's scheduled timeouts (node-wasm-host.ts:55-90).

The browser WASM profile loads the bridge in an in-realm path or a module worker; loadBrowserWasmHost/loadBrowserPersistentWasmHost spawn browser-wasm-worker.js/browser-content-worker.js (browser-wasm-host.ts:25-88).

WorkerEmbeddedHost bounds in-flight calls and bytes, reserves a control lane for stream cleanup (MAX_PENDING_CONTROLS=32), and rejects with EmbeddedStowError code "backpressure" when the limit is exceeded (worker-host.ts:31-58,143-150).

runWorkspaceCommand executes the resolved binary as [workspace, ...args] without a shell, decodes one JSON object from stdout, and handoffWorkspace with --output reads the document back from disk because the command prints nothing (workspace.ts:75-84,151-182).

serveWorkspace spawns `workspace serve --id ... --ready-fd 3 --parent-pid <pid>` with stdout ignored and reads a newline-terminated readiness object from descriptor 3, validating the required fields and version === 1 (workspace-serve.ts:25-88).

runDoctor merges client-side checks (binary resolution, platform package, node runtime) with the binary's own `doctor --json` report into one flat list and one ok flag; runDoctorCli exits non-zero on a required failure (doctor.ts:79-116,132-159,261-270).

upstreamFromEnv resolves endpoint/access/secret/sessionToken/region/bucket from the same env key lists, in the same STOW_* > S3_* > AWS_* order, as internal/runthrough/config.go FromEnv (upstream.ts:18-57 vs internal/runthrough/config.go:128-173).

The Go writer declares the same marker string, .stow-owner, as packages/stow-s3/src/ownership.ts:12; owner.go's cross-reference comment (owner.go:16) names packages/stow/src/ownership.ts, which is not the file that reads it.

The Python client's isolated-child prefixes are the tuple ("STOW_","S3_","AWS_") (session.py:50,63), the same three prefixes as start.ts's regex; it declares SESSION_GOGC="50" too (session.py:58), and its _server_args builds the same serve argv with --ready-fd and --parent-pid (session.py:254-274).

The repository gate compares SESSION_GOGC between start.ts and the Python session.py (check-version.mjs:169-183) and compares the ownership marker between internal/storage/fs/owner.go and src/ownership.ts (check-version.mjs:185-198); no gate covers the env-prefix set or the readiness protocol shape.

The site test reads src/index.ts as the export source of truth (SDK_SOURCE, examples.test.mjs:28) and fails when an example imports a name index.ts does not export (examples.test.mjs:60-81), so index.ts is consumed as a machine-checked interface.

interface.types: The root entry (package.json:8-12) exports a default Stow object with start(options?): Promise<StowInstance>, connect(options: ConnectOptions): StowConnection, awsSdkV3Config(options | instance): S3ClientConfig and upstream.fromEnv(): UpstreamConfig | null (index.ts:106-146), plus named exports: EmbeddedStow / EmbeddedStowError / EMBEDDED_PROTOCOL_VERSION (index.ts:14-18); loadNodeWasmHost and type NodeWasmHost (index.ts:23-26); resetOwnedData / STOW_OWNER_MARKER / StowOwnershipError (index.ts:29-33); openStow / withStow / DEFAULT_SESSION_MAX_BYTES / DEFAULT_SESSION_MAX_OBJECTS and the StowSession/StowSessionCapabilities/EphemeralStowOptions types (index.ts:59-69); parseReadyMessage / READY_PROTOCOL_VERSION / StowProtocolError and StowReady/StowReadyCapabilities (index.ts:70-78); resolveStowBinary / stowBinaryAvailable / StowBinaryNotFoundError (index.ts:79-83); parseReadyLine (index.ts:58); upstreamFromEnv (index.ts:84); twelve workspace functions (checkpointWorkspace, collectWorkspaces, pruneWorkspaces, destroyWorkspace, diffWorkspaces, exportWorkspaceCheckpoint, handoffWorkspace, importWorkspaceCheckpoint, prepareWorkspace, restoreWorkspaceCheckpoint, resumeWorkspace, runWorkspaceCommand) with their option types (index.ts:85-104); and serveWorkspace / ServeWorkspaceOptions / ServedWorkspace (index.ts:150-151). Public types include StartOptions and StowInstance (types.ts:15-77,134-152), AwsSdkV3ConfigOptions/ConnectOptions/StowConnection (types.ts:94-120), and EmbeddedHost/EmbeddedCapabilities/EmbeddedStowOptions (embedded.ts:9-88). Subpaths add the profiles: ./embedded, ./node-wasm, ./workspace, ./browser, ./browser-s3, ./worker, ./browser-wasm, ./project (package.json:13-45), and the stow-doctor bin.
invariants: A session's server is a child process this package owns; stop()/close() stop it, and a session created its own temp data dir removes it while a caller-supplied dataDir is preserved (session.ts:118-119,301-303; start.ts:267-273).

The server is told to write its readiness object to descriptor 3; the client never reads credentials from stdout when the versioned channel is used, and only a newline-terminated record is parsed (start.ts:174,293; ready-reader.ts:63,190-205).

STOW_BIN is overridden by an installed npm platform package; the platform-package and monorepo candidates are accepted only if executable, and a STOW_BIN path is returned by resolveStowBinaryDetailed without an executability test but rejected by stowBinaryAvailable when it is not executable (bin.ts:13-20,131-160).
The child environment is process.env verbatim for a long-lived server, and process.env minus STOW_*/S3_*/AWS_* only when isolatedEnvironment is set (start.ts:183-215).
GOGC is only defaulted to 50 when it is unset and the child is isolated; an explicit GOGC in the environment always wins (start.ts:204-206).
Region reported by the server in the readiness record is the region the client signs for; a default of us-east-1 applies only when the caller provides none (start.ts:314; instance.ts:66,108).
resetOwnedData never deletes a directory without the .stow-owner marker, nor the home directory or any ancestor of the working directory (ownership.ts:12,49-96).

Session.close is idempotent and returns the same promise, and every method after close throws an error with code "closed"; the dataDir getter (session.ts:223-225) and the s3 field remain readable (session.ts:277-319).
EmbeddedStow.close is idempotent and every verb after close throws EmbeddedStowError with code "closed" (embedded.ts:240-261).
The embedded protocol version is chosen from the host: JSON v1 when only call is present, binary v2 when callBinary is present (embedded.ts:1-2,264-282).
error_modes: StowBinaryNotFoundError (code "binary_not_found") when no runnable binary is found, with a searched order in the message (bin.ts:168-181); the message's stated order omits the installed platform package that actually outranks STOW_BIN.

StowProtocolError with code protocol_mismatch for a bad readiness version, non-object JSON, or a missing field; code cancelled when an AbortSignal aborts startup; code internal for a caller-supplied limit that is not a positive integer (ready.ts:38-48,82-127; start.ts:286,329-333).
StowOwnershipError (code "ownership") when resetOwnedData is asked to delete an unowned directory or a protected path (ownership.ts:15-22,83-96).
StowCredentialsError when neither static credentials nor a provider is supplied to the AWS config (instance.ts:33-62).
EmbeddedStowError with codes closed, host_error, protocol, protocol_version, conditional_write_unsupported and invalid_data (embedded.ts:107-115,171-176,248-316,368-376).

S3 operation failures arrive from the AWS SDK unchanged (Forbidden/AccessDenied, NoSuchKey, PreconditionFailed, InsufficientStorage) so callers keep matching on the SDK error; only session lifecycle failures use the local codes (ready.ts:33-38; test/session.test.ts:142-157; examples/stow-recipes/conditional-write.mjs:39-45).

On startup failure startStowWithReady stops the child before rethrowing (start.ts:321-323); openStow disposes the client, the instance and an owned data dir quietly before rethrowing (session.ts:159-163,322-345).
withStow rethrows the callback error and, if cleanup also fails, raises AggregateError carrying both and the cleanup cause (session.ts:169-191).
ordering: resetDataDirIfRequested runs before spawn, so a requested reset cannot race the server (start.ts:283).
The abort listener is installed after spawn and before waitForReady, so an abort at any stage stops the child (start.ts:300-306).
Startup buckets are created only after the readiness record is parsed and the instance exists, each under the remaining startup deadline (start.ts:217-229,319).
For a session, the generated bucket is created through the session's own client before openStow returns, so a failure surfaces before the caller's first operation (session.ts:148-152).
Session.close releases in the order client.destroy -> instance.stop -> rm(owned dataDir), each isolated so one failure does not abandon the others (session.ts:290-311).
handoff returns a new object per call so a caller cannot mutate the session's view (session.ts:253-275).
configuration: Environment inherited from the parent process, with STOW_*, S3_* and AWS_* removed only for an isolated session (start.ts:183-215).
STOW_BIN to point at a specific binary, outranked by an installed platform package (bin.ts:131-148).
STOW_LOCAL_ACCESS_KEY_ID and STOW_LOCAL_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY set on the child from StartOptions.accessKey/secretKey (start.ts:208-213).
GOGC defaulted to 50 for an isolated session when unset (start.ts:22,204-206).
Upstream credentials read from the environment with precedence STOW_* > S3_* > AWS_* (upstream.ts:17-57).

StartOptions: dataDir, backend (filesystem|memory), buckets, port, host, timeoutMs, signal, region, baseHost, allowPublicAdmin, resetOwnedData/cleanSlate, accessKey/secretKey, mode (local|run-through|auto), cacheDir, cacheMaxBytes, cacheMaxObjects, cacheTtlSeconds, allowLiveWrites, allowInsecureUpstream, maxRequestBytes, maxConcurrentRequests, maxBytes, maxObjects, isolatedEnvironment, parentPid (types.ts:15-77).
The npm export map and the stow-doctor bin field are the package's declared entry points and must resolve to dist/index.js, the subpath barrels and bin/stow-doctor.mjs (package.json:6-48).

implementation: The package is an ESM TypeScript library (type: module, package.json:5) built to dist/ and published to GitHub Packages (package.json:100-102). Node client core: start.ts resolves the binary (start.ts:267-273), builds the serve argv with --ready-fd READY_FD=3 and optional --parent-pid (start.ts:128-181), builds the child env with the isolated STOW_/S3_/AWS_ strip and the GOGC default (start.ts:183-215), spawns with a four-entry stdio (start.ts:291-295), and blocks on waitForReady (start.ts:306). ready-reader.ts owns the wire contract: it reads child.stdio[3], frames newline-terminated records (ready-framing.ts), caps a record at 256 KiB, falls back to the legacy STOW_READY stdout line with all capabilities reported as unknown, and distinguishes a closed descriptor from a child exit by a 50 ms grace (ready-reader.ts:51-59,63,190-253,263-275). ready.ts strictly validates the JSON object and its capabilities (ready.ts:82-127). instance.ts builds the AWS SDK v3 config (credentials provider wins over static, us-east-1 default, forcePathStyle true) and the StowInstance helpers createBucket/emptyBucket/putFixture/snapshotObjects (instance.ts:42-196); s3-client.ts adds the UNSIGNED_PAYLOAD build middleware (s3-client.ts:10-34). session.ts wraps that in a disposable session: mkdtemp when no dataDir is named, memory backend for a self-made dir and filesystem backend for a caller-named one, isolatedEnvironment true, parentPid = process.pid, generated bucket pre-created through the session client, an idempotent lazy close, and handoff() for a child process (session.ts:112-163,199-320). Embedded/WASM facade: embedded.ts speaks JSON v1 or binary v2 to a caller-supplied EmbeddedHost; node-wasm-host.ts loads wasm_exec.js and ./stow-runtime.wasm into the current realm and exposes the bridge; browser-wasm-host.ts loads the same runtime in a module worker or the current realm; wasm-bridge.ts and worker-host.ts define the async host contract with bounded in-flight calls. Profiles: browser.ts (IndexedDbPersistenceAdapter plus BrowserEmbeddedStow/BrowserFileHistory), worker.ts (AsyncEmbeddedStow, WorkerEmbeddedHost, serveEmbeddedWorker), project-library.ts (BrowserProject, ContentStore, IndexedDbContentAdapter, ContentObjectHost, migrateFileHistory), browser-s3.ts (S3ObjectSyncRemote over an AWS SDK S3Client). Binary resolution and the ownership guard: bin.ts holds the platform-package map and the four-rule precedence; ownership.ts holds STOW_OWNER_MARKER and the protected-path backstop. Workspace: workspace.ts shells `workspace` verbs with no shell and decodes one JSON object (or reads the --output document back); workspace-serve.ts spawns `workspace serve` and reads its own readiness object from fd 3. doctor.ts merges client-side checks with the binary's `doctor --json`. Callers: the four runnable example recipes (examples/stow-recipes/*.mjs), the site's example test which reads src/index.ts as the export source of truth (site/test/examples.test.mjs:28,60-81), the site's api-notes generator (site/api-notes.mjs), the npm-consumer smoke script (scripts/smoke-npm-consumer.mjs:2), and the package's own ~30 test files compiled against dist/. Duplication, stated factually: (1) upstream.ts:18-57 re-states the same env key list and STOW_* > S3_* > AWS_* order as internal/runthrough/config.go:129-172 FromEnv -- including the two identical AWS_ENDPOINT_URL* spellings and the STOW_BUCKET/S3_BUCKET pair; the native CLI itself holds no prefix rule, it reads each variable by name (internal/runthrough/config.go:176-227; cmd/stow-s3/main.go:210-217). (2) The prefix regex /^(STOW_|S3_|AWS_)/ at start.ts:191 has no Go counterpart; its cross-language twin is _ISOLATED_ENV_PREFIXES = ("STOW_","S3_","AWS_") in the Python client (packages/stow-s3-py/src/stow_s3/session.py:50,63), and the same prefix set is copied into benchmark and performance harnesses (benchmark/implementations.mjs:28; packages/stow-s3/scripts/performance/server.mjs:11). (3) SESSION_GOGC="50" (start.ts:22) duplicates the Python session.py:58 and is gated by scripts/check-version.mjs:169-183. (4) The ownership marker .stow-owner (ownership.ts:12) duplicates internal/storage/fs/owner.go:18 and is gated by scripts/check-version.mjs:185-198. (5) The readiness parser (ready.ts) and its protocol version duplicate the Go writer (cmd/stow-s3/main.go:47-94, internal/ready) and the Python reader (packages/stow-s3-py/src/stow_s3/ready.py:19,103). (6) The serve argv (start.ts:128-181) duplicates the Python _server_args (packages/stow-s3-py/src/stow_s3/session.py:254-274); neither argv carries a --read-only flag. (7) The binary-resolution order and the monorepo depth of 8 (bin.ts:44-60,131-148) duplicate packages/stow-s3-py/src/stow_s3/bin.py:22,89-103. (8) The stop sequence (start.ts:29-98) duplicates packages/stow-s3-py/src/stow_s3/session.py:192-205. The workspace wrapper enumerates twelve verbs while the native table has seventeen, including preview and adopt (cmd/stow-s3/workspace.go:119-137); four defined wrappers are not re-exported from index.ts.

callers.scope: withStow(fn) drives a real session round trip against a generated bucket
openStow({dataDir, bucket}) opens two sessions over one caller-owned directory to show persistence
withStow(fn) exercises the conditional-write refusal through the raw s3 client the session hands back
reads packages/stow-s3/src/index.ts as the export source of truth and asserts every example's imported symbol appears in it
embeds the package's documented imports and examples into the generated site pages
an npm consumer smoke test that imports openStow, prepareWorkspace and serveWorkspace from the package and drives a session plus a served workspace
the package's own test calls openStow/withStow and buildChildEnv/SESSION_GOGC from dist/session.js and dist/start.js
imports the root barrel (Stow, StowOwnershipError) and the shared S3 corpus to drive the public surface

depth_assessment.deletion_test: Delete packages/stow-s3 and the complexity does not vanish: it reappears in every consumer. Each of the example recipes, the site's example test, the npm-consumer smoke script and any npm consumer would have to re-implement binary resolution, spawn the serve child with the readiness descriptor, parse and strictly validate the readiness record, strip ambient cloud configuration, build the AWS SDK v3 client with UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD signing, own stop/reset/cleanup, and re-derive the embedded/WASM host protocol. The package's exported surface (a handful of functions and one default object) hides that entire lifecycle behind a single withStow call, which is the definition of a deep module. Some files inside it are thin (index.ts re-exports, browser.ts/worker.ts/project-library.ts barrels), but the unit's depth is carried by start.ts/ready-reader.ts/ready.ts/instance.ts/session.ts and the embedded facade.

leverage: Callers get one call -- withStow(fn) or openStow() -- that returns a ready AWS SDK S3 client, a generated bucket, generated credentials and a region, with process lifecycle, readiness handshake, ambient-config isolation and cleanup all handled behind it, and a parallel embedded()/worker()/browser()/project() surface for hosts with no binary. They do not encode the readiness protocol, the argv the server expects, the env strip, the binary search order or the ownership rule; they supply only options and an S3 client.
locality: Maintainers get one package where each concern lives in one file: start.ts owns the process lifecycle and child env, ready-reader.ts/ready-framing.ts/ready.ts own the wire contract, instance.ts/s3-client.ts own the AWS wiring, bin.ts owns binary resolution, ownership.ts owns the reset guard, and workspace.ts owns the CLI veneer. The cost is that the shared contracts are not local: the env-prefix set, the readiness protocol version, the ownership marker, the session GOGC, the serve argv and the binary search order each also exist in the Python client or the Go writer, so a change here is only correct once the other side moves too -- and only GOGC and the ownership marker are guarded by scripts/check-version.mjs.
risks: The public root surface is not the same as the package's implemented surface: listWorkspaces, adoptWorkspaceHandoff, createWorkspaceDelta and applyWorkspaceDelta are defined in src/workspace.ts (workspace.ts:113,190,197,204) but are reachable only through the "./workspace" subpath, so a caller reading index.ts as the API will not find four of the seventeen native verbs (cmd/stow-s3/workspace.go:119-137).

The npm platform package deliberately outranks STOW_BIN (bin.ts:122-148), so a caller who upgrades the package and keeps an exported STOW_BIN silently gets the installed binary rather than the one they named; the only way to force a build is a tree with no platform package installed.

When the server does not honour --ready-fd and writes the legacy STOW_READY line, every capability in the synthesized StowReady is reported as unknown (persistent/multipart/upstream all false, limits all 0) (ready-reader.ts:79-100), and session.capabilities() would then report maxBytes 0; the protocol documents 0 as "no limit reported" rather than unlimited (ready.ts, session.ts:232-251), so a caller must branch on backend/protocolVersion rather than on the numbers.

Endpoint and credentials are taken from the child's readiness record (start.ts:307-318), so the trust boundary is the pipe: any server able to write to descriptor 3 supplies the credentials the caller's S3 client will then sign with.

The ownership reset guard is a two-sided constant with the Go writer only because scripts/check-version.mjs:185-198 compares the two string literals; a value change on both sides that the regex still matches would pass the gate, and the gate says nothing about the marker's payload version (owner.go:22).

priority.rationale: Blast radius is every consumer of the published package plus the repository's examples, site tests and npm-consumer smoke script, and the unit carries the child-process and readiness contracts that three languages must agree on. A defect breaks sessions rather than a single feature, and the cross-language duplicates (env-prefix set, serve argv, binary order, readiness shape) are hidden coupling that only scripts/check-version.mjs:169-198 partially guards. It is not P1 because it is a client library over a local loopback server and no defect is demonstrated; the one destructive path, resetOwnedData, is marker-guarded and fails by refusing.

next_action: Document the exec/env contract and align the exported surface with the implemented one. Add a doc comment on StartOptions (types.ts:15) and StowSession (session.ts:35) stating the facts a caller must currently infer from source: the server is spawned as `serve` with --ready-fd 3 and optional --parent-pid, the child environment is process.env with STOW_*/S3_*/AWS_* removed only under isolatedEnvironment, GOGC defaults to 50 only there, and the credentials come from descriptor 3. Re-export listWorkspaces, adoptWorkspaceHandoff, createWorkspaceDelta and applyWorkspaceDelta from src/index.ts so the root surface matches src/workspace.ts, and extend scripts/check-version.mjs to check the env-prefix set and the serve-argv spellings against packages/stow-s3-py. The concrete interfaces that would change are packages/stow-s3/src/index.ts (four new named exports) and the StartOptions/StowSession doc comments; in the Go tree, correct the cross-reference at internal/storage/fs/owner.go:16 from packages/stow/src/ownership.ts to packages/stow-s3/src/ownership.ts.

title: pkg/stow/capacity.go is a pass-through wrapper over internal/capacity, not a module
claimed_root_cause: Candidate: a public module exposing capacity budgeting — a trusted host that binds namespaces with their own byte budgets and a recovery reserve, surfaced as stow.CapacityHost and stow.CapacityNamespace.

trace.scope: OpenCapacityHost forwards one call to capacity.Open and boxes the returned *capacity.Host in the wrapper struct (:29-33).
(*CapacityHost).BindNamespace forwards one call to the inner host's Bind after a nil-receiver guard (:37-39), boxing *capacity.Namespace (:40-44).
(*CapacityNamespace).Snapshot forwards to the inner namespace's Snapshot after a nil-receiver guard (:48-50); the forwarding lands on internal/capacity/accounting.go:130.

evidence.detail: Three type aliases onto internal/capacity: CapacityHostOptions=capacity.HostOptions (:10), CapacityNamespaceOptions=capacity.NamespaceOptions (:11), CapacitySnapshot=capacity.Snapshot (:12).

Five error aliases: ErrCapacityFull/Invalid/Conflict/Unknown = capacity.ErrFull/ErrInvalid/ErrConflict/ErrUnknown (:15-18) and ErrRecoveryHeld = storage.ErrRecoveryHeld (:21), a cross-package alias to internal/storage, not to internal/capacity.

CapacityHost and CapacityNamespace are one-field structs, each holding a single unexported pointer to the internal type; the file's own comment at :24 says the host configures trusted namespace budgets and does not authenticate callers.

Snapshot forwards to the inner namespace and refuses a nil receiver with ErrCapacityInvalid (:48-50). The only other conditionals in the 52-line file are BindNamespace's nil guard (:37-39) and the two error propagations (:30-32, :41-43); there is no domain branching.

Where the host behaviour actually lives: capacity.Open validates the host options (Dir, MaxBytes, MaxNamespaces, GOOS) at :21-29 and writes the initial state at :35; capacity.(*Host).Bind validates and persists a namespace at :39-66.

The real Snapshot implementation; the byte/recovery accounting is namespaceCharge at accounting.go:31-56, and admission decisions are in admission.go, operations.go and state.go — all in internal/capacity, which has its own unit in this run.

FilesystemOptions.Namespace is the only production-visible naming of the wrapper type; it is dereferenced by openFilesystemStore (pkg/stow/filesystem_native.go:43-46, which passes options.Namespace.inner to fs.NewFilesystemStoreWithNamespace) and guarded against a nil inner at filesystem_native.go:18-19.

The only caller of OpenCapacityHost in the repository (stow.OpenCapacityHost at :18, host.BindNamespace at :22). FilesystemOptions.Namespace is set only in this test file (:55, :136); no production caller constructs a namespace.

reason: Pass-through, not a module. pkg/stow/capacity.go is 52 lines: three type aliases (:10-12), five error aliases (:15-21), two one-field structs holding an unexported pointer (:25-26), and three functions that each forward a single call — OpenCapacityHost (:28-34), BindNamespace (:36-45) and Snapshot (:47-52). It holds no domain branching; its only conditionals are two nil-receiver guards returning ErrCapacityInvalid (:37-39, :48-50) and two error propagations (:30-32, :41-43). Every decision the candidate attributes to it — the byte budget, the recovery reserve, the accounting — is owned by internal/capacity: Open (state.go:20), Bind (state.go:39), Snapshot (accounting.go:130) and namespaceCharge (accounting.go:31), and internal/capacity has its own unit in this run. The deletion test goes the 'vanishes' way. Deleting pkg/stow/capacity.go does not concentrate any complexity across callers, because the only caller of OpenCapacityHost in the whole tree is the package's own test (object_recovery_test.go:18, :22), and the budget logic would live in internal/capacity either way; what remains in the callers is the trivial removal of a type name. The wrapper adds exactly two things internal/capacity does not: a nil-receiver guard that returns ErrCapacityInvalid, and a public type that FilesystemOptions.Namespace can name (filesystem.go:6, consumed at filesystem_native.go:18-19 and :43-46). A nil guard is not an implementation that holds decisions, and the public type is the pkg/stow public-surface module (its own unit in this run), not a module of this file. Rejected: a pass-through wrapper over another package's implementation, with no production caller and no complexity of its own.

title: Checkpoint archives and handoff bundles
summary: The transfer module: turning a retained checkpoint into a portable archive, verifying an archive before it is imported, and packaging both into a handoff bundle that another machine can adopt. It owns the rules that an archive carries checkpoint bytes and metadata only and never registry state or credentials, that a received archive is verified against a published digest before a single byte of it is trusted, that an import is staged privately and published only after every path and digest has passed, and that a handoff bundle is published by an atomic no-replace rename so a destination is never overwritten.

trace.scope: ExportHandoff is the entry point for producing a portable bundle from a workspace and one of its checkpoints.
The checkpoint is loaded and checked to belong to the named workspace before anything is written.
exportHandoffArchive writes the checkpoint into a staged checkpoint.tar.gz and digests the bytes as they are written.
handoff.json is written beside the archive, naming the workspace, the checkpoint and the archive's digest and size.
publishHandoffDirectory renames the staged bundle into place with a no-replace rename; this is the point at which the bundle becomes visible.

evidence.detail: ExportCheckpoint writes a gzip tar of the manifest and the payload files, under a capture lock, and includes only checkpoint bytes and metadata.
PreviewCheckpointArchive validates the archive structure, the paths, the limits, the content digests and the gzip trailer without extracting or publishing anything.
validateArchiveSensitiveFiles refuses an export that contains a credential-looking path unless the caller opted in.
ImportCheckpoint extracts into a private .import- staging directory inside the checkpoint store and removes it on any failure.
publishImportedCheckpoint refuses a checkpoint id that already exists, so an import never replaces a retained checkpoint.
verifiedHandoffSource copies the archive to a private temporary file, checks its size and SHA-256 against the reference, and only then hands the copy to the importer.
ReadHandoff requires a regular file of at most 1 MiB and the decoder refuses unknown fields and trailing data.
adoptHandoff imports first and restores second, so a failed restore still returns the imported checkpoint rather than losing it.
On Linux the bundle is published with renameat2 and RENAME_NOREPLACE, so an existing destination is refused rather than replaced.

interface.types: stow.CheckpointArchiveOptions{MaxBytes, MaxFiles, IncludeSensitiveFiles, ExpectedSHA256} bounds archive work; zero takes the conservative defaults. stow.CheckpointArchivePreview is the verified description of an archive, including the sensitive-looking paths it would import. stow.Handoff is the reference document{Version, WorkspaceID, CheckpointID, RegistryDir, Team, Archive *stow.HandoffArchive{Path, SHA256, Bytes, Files}}; stow.HandoffExportOptions{RegistryDir, WorkspaceID, CheckpointID, BundleDir, ArchiveOptions} is the export input. stow.HandoffError{BundleDir, Outcome, Err} is the typed failure for a bundle whose durability outcome is unknown.
invariants: An archive carries checkpoint bytes and metadata only, never workspace credentials or registry state (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:63).
A credential-looking path requires an explicit export opt-in, and the refusal names the path (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:304).

A received archive is verified against the digest the reference published before it is imported; a mismatch against that published digest is refused with "handoff archive digest does not match reference" (pkg/stow/handoff.go:289). The caller's out-of-band ExpectedSHA256 is a second, independent check, and its mismatch is ErrHandoffDigestMismatch (pkg/stow/handoff.go:292).
The archive is copied to a private temporary file and that copy is what is imported, so a source that changes mid-read cannot be half-read (pkg/stow/handoff.go:273).
An import publishes only after every path, size and digest has been checked in the staging directory (pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:66).
An import refuses an id that already exists rather than replacing a retained checkpoint (pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:223).
The handoff document's identity must match the archive's: a preview whose workspace or checkpoint differs from the document is refused (pkg/stow/handoff.go:171).
A bundle is published by a no-replace rename, so an existing destination is never overwritten (pkg/stow/handoff_publish.go:20, pkg/stow/handoff_rename_darwin.go:6).
The reference document is bounded to 1 MiB and must contain exactly one JSON value with no unknown fields (pkg/stow/handoff.go:105, pkg/stow/handoff.go:120).
error_modes: "stow: checkpoint archive input is required" and "stow: checkpoint archive output is required" (pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:23, pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:67).
"stow: checkpoint archive limits must not be negative" (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:205).

"stow: checkpoint archive file %q failed integrity validation" and the missing-files refusal when the archive does not carry every expected file (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:194, pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:198).
"stow: checkpoint archive must begin with a bounded manifest.json" and "stow: unsupported or invalid checkpoint archive" (pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:104, pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:129).

"stow: checkpoint %s already exists" on an import (pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:223) and "stow: checkpoint %q already exists" on a delta publish that would replace a retained checkpoint (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:268).
"handoff archive digest does not match reference" and "handoff archive size does not match reference" (pkg/stow/handoff.go:290, pkg/stow/handoff.go:271).
"stow: handoff identity does not match its archive" (pkg/stow/handoff.go:172).
"unsupported handoff reference version %d" and "invalid handoff reference: no workspace id" (pkg/stow/handoff.go:133, pkg/stow/handoff.go:136).
"stow: atomic handoff directory publication is unsupported on this platform" on a host that is neither Linux nor Darwin (pkg/stow/handoff_rename_other.go:8).
A *stow.HandoffError with outcome unknown when the bundle was published but the parent directory could not be fsynced (pkg/stow/handoff_publish.go:24).
ordering: Export stages the bundle in a temporary directory beside the destination and only renames it into place at the end, so a partial bundle is never visible (pkg/stow/handoff.go:61, pkg/stow/handoff.go:85).
The archive is written and digested before handoff.json is written, so the document always describes a complete archive (pkg/stow/handoff.go:66, pkg/stow/handoff.go:76).
The tree is fsynced before the rename, so the bytes are durable before they become visible (pkg/stow/handoff.go:79).
Import verifies the archive, then previews it, then imports it, and the identity comparison happens before the import (pkg/stow/handoff.go:167, pkg/stow/handoff.go:171).
AdoptHandoff imports before it restores, so the checkpoint survives a failed restore (pkg/stow/handoff.go:228, pkg/stow/handoff.go:233).
configuration: MaxBytes and MaxFiles bound the archive; zero takes the conservative defaults of 1 GiB and 100000 files rather than meaning unlimited (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:310, pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:317).
IncludeSensitiveFiles is the opt-in that lets a credential-looking path travel in an archive (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:36).
ExpectedSHA256 is an optional second digest the receiver can insist on, checked independently of the digest embedded in the reference (pkg/stow/handoff.go:292).

The bundle's location is the caller's choice: BundleDir names the directory the bundle is published as, and a relative archive path is resolved against the reference document's own directory (pkg/stow/handoff.go:248).
The registry directory and team are the caller's choice, and a handoff's team must not conflict with the destination team (pkg/stow/handoff.go:218).

implementation: ExportHandoff (pkg/stow/handoff.go:46) checks the workspace exists, loads the checkpoint and checks it belongs to that workspace, stages a temporary directory beside the requested bundle directory, writes checkpoint.tar.gz through ExportCheckpoint while digesting it, writes handoff.json naming the workspace, checkpoint and archive digest and size, fsyncs the tree and renames the staged directory into place through publishHandoffDirectory, which is a no-replace rename on Linux and Darwin and a refusal elsewhere. The publication error carries the bundle directory and the outcome so a caller that cannot tell whether the bundle landed can find it. ImportCheckpoint (pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:21) creates the checkpoint store, extracts into a private .import- staging directory, validates the manifest strictly (the decoder refuses unknown fields and trailing data), extracts each file with O_EXCL and verifies its digest, verifies the gzip trailer is empty, verifies the whole staged payload, takes the mutation-capture lock, refuses an existing id, applies the registry admission check and only then publishes by rename. PreviewCheckpointArchive (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:108) does the same verification without extracting, and additionally reports the sensitive-looking paths it would import so a caller can decide. The handoff receive path (pkg/stow/handoff.go:148) resolves the archive path relative to the reference document, copies the archive to a private temporary file while hashing it, compares the size and the digest against the reference, and then previews and imports that copy. adoptHandoff (pkg/stow/handoff.go:208) validates the document, refuses a destination that already exists, refuses a team conflict, resolves the destination registry, imports the archive and then restores the checkpoint into a new workspace, returning the imported checkpoint information even when the restore fails.

callers.scope: The CLI's `workspace preview` verb calls stow.PreviewCheckpointArchive to show an archive's contents before anything is imported.
The `workspace export` verb calls stow.ExportCheckpoint to write the archive file.
The `workspace import` verb calls stow.ImportCheckpoint to publish an imported archive as a retained checkpoint.
The CLI's handoff verbs call stow.ImportHandoff, which verifies the archive against the reference before importing it.
The CLI reads a handoff reference through stow.ReadHandoff, so the reference's own bound and strict decoding apply.
The MCP handoff export tool calls stow.ExportHandoff with the configured bounds and the configured export root.

The MCP handoff adopt tool calls stow.AdoptHandoffArchive with the already-opened archive and the caller's expected digest, and reports a partial import when the restore failed after a successful import.

depth_assessment.deletion_test: The complexity concentrates in the callers. Deleting this module would push the transfer contract into the CLI and the MCP server: that an archive carries bytes and metadata only (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:63), that a received archive must be verified against a published digest before it is trusted (pkg/stow/handoff.go:289), that an import is staged privately and published only after every digest has passed (pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go:60), and that a bundle is published by a no-replace rename so an existing destination is never overwritten (pkg/stow/handoff_publish.go:20). Each is a rule a caller re-implementing the transfer would get wrong in a way that only shows up across machines, which is exactly where the caller cannot test it.

leverage: A caller gets a portable, self-describing bundle and a verified import for one call each, and it inherits the path rules, the sensitive-path rules and the manifest validation the checkpoint store already owns rather than re-deriving them. A receiver that knows only the published digest can refuse a tampered bundle, and the refusal is a named error rather than a corrupted workspace. The same archive format serves the CLI's export/import verbs, the handoff verbs and the MCP handoff tools.
locality: The archive format lives in pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go and pkg/stow/checkpoint_import.go; the bundle and the reference document live in pkg/stow/handoff.go and pkg/stow/handoff_publish.go, with the platform-specific rename isolated in three one-function files. The rules that must not drift — the sensitive-path list and the manifest validation — are shared with the checkpoint store, so a change there moves both. The bundle's durability depends on the platform's rename semantics, which is why the rename is behind three build-tagged implementations.
risks: The bundle's publication has an unknown-outcome state: if the rename succeeds but the parent directory cannot be fsynced, the error is a HandoffError with outcome unknown (pkg/stow/handoff_publish.go:24) and the bundle may or may not exist. A caller that treats the error as a failure may publish a second bundle under a different name.

A relative archive path in the reference document is resolved against the reference document's own directory (pkg/stow/handoff.go:248), so a reference that is moved without its archive names a different file; the digest check catches it, but the error names a size or digest mismatch rather than a moved bundle.

The archive's byte and file limits (CheckpointArchiveOptions) are independent of the checkpoint capture's own limits, and the portable manifest is separately held to fixed format bounds that no archive option raises (pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable.go:140), so raising MaxFiles does not raise the format bound a large archive must satisfy.

Handoff version 1 is a same-machine reference (a workspace id plus a registry directory) and version 2 carries an archive; ValidateHandoff accepts both (pkg/stow/handoff.go:132). The two are consumed through different paths: a version-1 document is read by the CLI resume path, which takes document.RegistryDir (cmd/stow-s3/workspace.go:371), while a version-2 document is imported by ImportHandoff/adopt, which refuses a document that carries no archive (pkg/stow/handoff.go:241). A reader of the Handoff struct cannot tell from the type which shape a given document is.

priority.rationale: Impact is P2 because the module is the cross-machine path and its blast radius is the CLI's export, import, preview and handoff verbs plus the MCP handoff tools, all of which share the archive format and the digest rule. Overall is P2 because the risks are localised and mostly about a state a caller must handle rather than about a defect: the unknown publication outcome, the relative-path resolution, and the two handoff document versions taking different code paths.

next_action: State the bundle's contract where a reader will find it: pkg/stow/handoff.go:28 defines the reference document, and the fact that version 1 is a same-machine reference consumed by the CLI resume path (cmd/stow-s3/workspace.go:371) while version 2 carries an archive imported by ImportHandoff (pkg/stow/handoff.go:148, pkg/stow/handoff.go:241) is not visible from the type. The interface that should change is Handoff, whose Version field selects between two incompatible shapes; a reader of the struct cannot tell which one a given document will be, and the path they must take differs with it.

title: Checkpoint capture, store and comparison
summary: The checkpoint module: capturing an immutable snapshot of a workspace, retaining it in the registry's checkpoint store, loading and validating it back, comparing two of them, and restoring one into a new workspace. It owns the durability contract that a checkpoint becomes visible only by a rename, that a tree which changed during the capture is refused rather than snapshotted, that the retention caps are exact because the capture lock is held across the check, and that a checkpoint can be captured from outside a workspace handle without claiming its session.

trace.scope: Workspace.CreateCheckpoint is the entry point for a capture taken through a workspace handle.
The capture is authorised against the workspace root before the lock is taken, so a refusal costs nothing and holds nothing.
The mutation-capture lock is claimed for the workspace, which is what makes the retention caps exact under parallel captures.
The tree is scanned for regular files, each with a SHA-256, under the caller's byte and file caps.
The scanned files are copied into a staging directory and each copy is re-digested, so a file that changed mid-copy is refused.
The tree is scanned again and compared with the first scan, so a workspace that changed during the capture is refused.
The staged directory is renamed into <registry>/checkpoints/<id>; the rename is the visibility boundary, and a failure after it is reported as outcome_unknown.

evidence.detail: addRegularFile refuses a symbolic link and any non-regular file, and enforces the byte and file caps during the walk rather than after it.
copyCheckpointInput compares the digest of the bytes it just wrote with the digest the scan recorded, and raises a workspace_changed failure when they disagree.
LoadCheckpoint decodes with DisallowUnknownFields and rejects a trailing JSON value, an unsupported version and an id that does not match the one asked for.
validCheckpointPath refuses an absolute path, a backslash, a parent traversal, a .git segment and a leading .stow segment.
checkCheckpointRetention counts only published checkpoints and refuses a new one that would pass the count or the byte cap, folding both into the same capacity_exceeded failure shape.
CheckpointOfAuthorized captures a workspace another process may be using right now: it does not claim the session and writes only into the checkpoint store.
newCheckpointReceipt derives the checkpoint id from a digest of the workspace id and the request key, so the same request key always names the same checkpoint.
resolveCheckpointReceipt refuses a retained receipt whose identity or options disagree with the request, and reports the outcome as unknown rather than absent.
checkpointFailure carries a code, a phase and an outcome, and classifyCheckpointError maps a lock-in-progress, an unsupported lock, a cancellation and a permission error onto distinct codes.
The package's own test asserts that a credential-looking file and Git metadata are excluded from a capture and that the excluded list names what was dropped.

interface.types: stow.CheckpointOptions{MaxBytes, MaxFiles, IncludeSensitiveFiles, ParentID, PortableObjects}. stow.CheckpointManifest is the persisted document: Version, ID, WorkspaceID, ParentID, Created, Files ([]stow.CheckpointFile{Path, Size, Mode, SHA256}), Excluded, WorkingDirectory, and for the portable form also Provenance, PrimaryBucket, Buckets, Objects ([]stow.CheckpointObject) and Payloads. stow.CheckpointInfo is the summary returned to callers. stow.CheckpointChange and stow.PortableCheckpointDiff are the comparison results. stow.CheckpointRequest{Key, Options, Hold} and stow.CheckpointResult{Checkpoint, Replayed, Outcome} are the request-replay surface. stow.CheckpointError is the typed failure with Code, Phase, Attempts, Retryable, Outcome and the wrapped Err.
invariants: A checkpoint becomes visible only by a rename into <registry>/checkpoints/<id>; a reader never sees a partial checkpoint (pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:47).
The source tree is scanned before and after the copy and the two scans must agree, or the capture is refused as workspace_changed (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:196, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:77).
Each copied file's digest is verified against the digest the scan recorded (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:183).

Stow metadata (.stow) and Git internals (.git) are always excluded; credential-looking paths are excluded unless the caller opts in (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:87, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:79).

The retention caps count published checkpoints only, and the check happens under the capture lock, so two parallel captures cannot both pass the same remaining capacity (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:111, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:90).
A parent checkpoint must exist and belong to the same workspace (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:233).
A manifest's id must equal the id it was asked for, its version must be supported, and every path must be safe and unique (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:270, pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:294).
A capture from outside a workspace does not claim the session and consults no policy unless a principal is named explicitly (pkg/stow/checkpoint_external.go:53, pkg/stow/checkpoint_external.go:92).

A request key names exactly one checkpoint: the id is derived from the digest of the workspace id and the key, and a retained receipt whose options disagree with the request is a conflict (pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:98, pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:149).
error_modes: A *stow.CheckpointError with code capacity_exceeded when a scan or the admission check exceeds the byte or file cap (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:112, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:110).
A *stow.CheckpointError with code workspace_changed when the tree changed during the capture (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:184, pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:196).
A *stow.CheckpointError with code outcome_unknown when the state after the rename cannot be established, which the caller must not retry blindly (pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:52).
A *stow.CheckpointError with code invalid_parent when the named parent does not belong to the workspace (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:138).

A *stow.CheckpointError with code request_conflict when a retained receipt disagrees with the request or an aborted hold is reactivated (pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:150, pkg/stow/checkpoint_recovery_hold.go:31).

A capture lock already held surfaces as in_progress on the request path, where classification is applied (pkg/stow/checkpoint_error.go:40, pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:65); CreateCheckpoint and CheckpointOf(Authorized) return the raw workspace.ErrCaptureInProgress instead, because they do not call classifyCheckpointError. in_progress is the only code marked Retryable (pkg/stow/checkpoint_error.go:27).
"stow: checkpoint %s has an unsupported or mismatched manifest" and "stow: decode checkpoint %s" when a manifest is malformed (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:271, pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:265).
"stow: invalid checkpoint id %q" for an id that is not 27 characters of the cp_ form (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:416).
ordering: Authorise, then take the capture lock, then scan, then stage, then copy, then re-verify, then publish (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:97, pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:100, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:47, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:62, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:67, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:77, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:80).
The retention check happens before the copy, under the same lock, so a capture that would exceed a cap costs a scan and not a copy (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:59).

The published manifest is written into the staging directory and the whole tree is fsynced before the rename, so the rename publishes bytes that are already durable (pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:35, pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:38).

A capture must not be taken while another process holds the workspace session; the session lock and the capture lock are different locks and the capture lock is the one the retention arithmetic depends on (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:82, pkg/stow/checkpoint_external.go:97).

Restore reopens the checkpoint twice, once before the lock and once after it, and verifies the payload digests before any file is written (pkg/stow/checkpoint_restore.go:26, pkg/stow/checkpoint_restore.go:30).
configuration: MaxBytes and MaxFiles bound a single capture; zero means unbounded for the capture itself (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:30, pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:151).
IncludeSensitiveFiles opts in to credential-looking paths; the default excludes them and reports them in the Excluded list (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:79).
ParentID chains a checkpoint to a parent; the parent must belong to the same workspace (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:31).

PortableObjects switches the capture from a file-only manifest to the version-2 form that also records logical objects and their payloads (pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable.go:17, pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable_capture.go:18).

The workspace's own MaxCheckpointBytes and MaxCheckpoints caps come from the registry entry, not from the caller, so a capture from outside the handle enforces the same limits (pkg/stow/checkpoint_external.go:23).

implementation: captureCheckpoint (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:32) is the one capture path; the handle path and the outside-the-handle path differ only in how they are authorised and in where the target's directory and caps come from. It validates the parent, opens the source through internal/rooted so no path component can be a symlink, scans the tree for regular files with a digest and size each (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:36), applies the caller's caps during the walk, checks the registry and workspace retention caps under the capture lock (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:91), stages into a .checkpoint- temporary directory inside the checkpoint store, copies the files concurrently with eight workers while re-digesting each one (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go:139), stages the manifest (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:118), re-scans the tree and compares it with the first scan, and only then publishes by writing the manifest, fsyncing the tree and renaming the staged directory into place (pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:30). A failure after the rename is reported with outcome unknown, because the durable outcome genuinely is not knowable at that point. The portable form adds a logical object scan (pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable.go:43), a payload copy and a second comparison of the logical snapshot and the provenance (pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable_capture.go:45). LoadCheckpoint is the inverse: it bounds the manifest read, decodes it strictly, refuses an unknown version, a mismatched id, an unsafe or repeated path and bad file metadata (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:279), and every read of a checkpoint's bytes goes through a reader that refuses a symlink anywhere in the path and re-verifies the digest (pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:127). The request surface derives a checkpoint id from the request key, writes a receipt into the staged directory, and on a replay compares the retained receipt with the request before reporting the earlier result (pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:38, pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:72, pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:149).

callers.scope: The CLI's `workspace checkpoint` verb calls stow.CheckpointOfAuthorized, so a checkpoint of a live workspace does not require the agent to stop.
The `workspace diff` verb calls stow.CompareCheckpoints to name what changed between two checkpoints.
The `workspace restore` verb calls stow.RestoreCheckpoint to seed a new workspace from a retained checkpoint.
The CLI's capture-request verb calls stow.CaptureCheckpoint or stow.ResolveCheckpoint with a caller-supplied request key, and reports the typed CheckpointError to the caller.
The MCP capture tool calls stow.CaptureCheckpoint and the resolve tool calls stow.ResolveCheckpoint, so a retry after a crash replays the earlier result rather than capturing again.
CreateDelta loads both endpoints through LoadCheckpoint, so the delta format is defined against the same manifest the checkpoint store owns.
ExportCheckpoint loads the manifest through LoadCheckpoint and re-reads it under a capture lock, so the archive format is defined against the same manifest.
CreateHandoff loads the manifest through LoadCheckpoint and counts its payloads, so a handoff bundle is bound to the checkpoint store's document.
The `workspace resume` verb loads a checkpoint manifest through stow.LoadCheckpoint to refuse a handoff checkpoint that belongs to a different workspace.
The package's own test asserts the exclusion rules of a capture.

depth_assessment.deletion_test: The complexity concentrates in the callers rather than vanishing. Deleting the checkpoint module would push the durability contract into every caller that stores bytes: the scan-and-re-verify rule that refuses a changed tree (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:196), the rename-as-visibility-boundary rule (pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:47), the retention caps that must be checked under a lock to be exact (pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go:90), the manifest validation that makes a path safe to extract (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:305), and the request-replay identity rule (pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:98). Five dependent features - the checkpoint store, the archive path (pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:75), the handoff path (pkg/stow/handoff.go:51), the delta path (pkg/stow/delta.go:174) and the restore path (pkg/stow/checkpoint_restore.go:13) - would each have to re-derive them, and they would not agree, because the whole point of the shared manifest and the shared lock is that they do.

leverage: A caller gets a snapshot it can trust, a store it can compare against, and a format it can transport, from one vocabulary: the same manifest, the same file records, the same path rules and the same digests serve the checkpoint store, the archive, the handoff bundle and the delta document. A caller that needs to retry a capture after a crash gets replay rather than a second capture for free, and a caller that captures a live workspace gets a refusal instead of a torn snapshot.
locality: The capture and store rules live in pkg/stow/checkpoint.go, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture.go, pkg/stow/checkpoint_capture_core.go and pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go; the request and hold rules live in pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go and pkg/stow/checkpoint_recovery_hold.go; the portable form lives in pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable.go and pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable_capture.go. The path rules are shared with the seed (pkg/stow/prepare_seed.go:16) and the delta validator (pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:49), the sensitive-path list is shared with the seed (pkg/stow/prepare_seed.go:144), and the reader that refuses symlinks is shared with the delta (pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:127). The persisted layout is <registry>/checkpoints/<id>/{manifest.json,files/...}, which is the contract every reader in the tree depends on.
risks: A capture that fails after the rename reports outcome unknown (pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:52) and the receipt-based resolve path reports the same (pkg/stow/checkpoint_request.go:167), so a caller must be able to distinguish 'not committed' from 'unknown' or it will retry a capture that may already exist.

The manifest's format version is carried in a field that the portable form reuses for a different shape (pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable.go:17), and CompareCheckpoints refuses a portable checkpoint with a message naming a different function (pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:369). A caller that compares the wrong pair of checkpoints gets a redirect rather than a comparison.

CheckpointOf consults no policy and passes authority.All() (pkg/stow/checkpoint_external.go:58); the module's own comment says callers relying on that should say so at the call site rather than assume a gate is present, which makes the safe usage a convention rather than a rule.

The retention caps are per workspace and per registry, and the registry-wide count is recomputed by loading every retained manifest (pkg/stow/registry_policy.go:54). The cost of an admission check therefore grows with the number of retained checkpoints.

priority.rationale: Impact is P1 because this module is the durability core that four other features and two surfaces depend on: the checkpoint store, the portable archive, the handoff bundle, the delta document, the CLI's checkpoint verbs and the MCP capture tools all share its manifest, its path rules and its lock discipline, so a change to any of them breaks the rest. Overall is P1 because the risk is demonstrated rather than hypothetical: the outcome-unknown path is a real branch a caller must handle, the portable and file-only manifests share a version field, and the admission check is O(retained checkpoints) on every capture.

next_action: Document the manifest as the shared contract rather than as an internal detail: pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:42 defines a shape that the archive, the handoff, the delta and the restore all depend on, and the version field that distinguishes the portable form (pkg/stow/checkpoint_portable.go:17) is the one place a future format change would break all five at once. The interface that should change is CheckpointOptions: PortableObjects changes the manifest version, the file list and the payload set, and the option name does not say so, so a caller that sets it has to know it is choosing a different format rather than a different scope.

title: Delta documents
summary: The delta module: describing the difference between two checkpoints as a versioned, self-contained document that carries the bytes of every changed path, transporting it, and applying it to a third point. It owns the conflict rule that a target which is neither the delta's from-state nor its to-state is refused rather than merged, the digest rule that binds the change list and not merely the content bytes, and the ordering rule that every precondition is checked before any byte is written.

trace.scope: CreateDelta is the exported entry point for describing the difference between two checkpoints in one registry.
The two checkpoints must belong to the same workspace, so a delta can never cross a workspace boundary.
A capture lock is taken for the workspace and both manifests are reloaded under it, so the two manifests cannot move under the comparison.
recordDeltaChanges walks the sorted union of paths and attaches the bytes of every added or changed path, enforcing the bounds as it goes.
EncodeDelta validates and serialises the document; DeltaDocumentDigest (pkg/stow/delta.go:359) digests exactly those bytes, which is what binds the change list to the sender's intent.
publishCheckpointContext publishes the replayed tree into <registry>/checkpoints/<id> by rename (pkg/stow/checkpoint_publish.go:48), publishing the new checkpoint.

evidence.detail: attach reads a path's bytes out of the target checkpoint and verifies the digest the manifest claims, so a delta whose content disagrees with its own description cannot be produced.
DeltaDocumentDigest hashes the encoded bytes, so the digest covers the change list, the paths, the kinds, the metadata and the content together.
checkDeltaSize counts the content the document actually carries rather than the Bytes field it declares, because a declaration is a claim and the map is the evidence.
ApplyDeltaWithOptions verifies every precondition before it writes anything, because a delta applied half way is a target that matches neither end.
checkDeltaPrecondition is the conflict rule: an added path asserts absence, a changed path asserts the exact from-state, and a divergence is ErrDeltaConflict rather than a merge.
applyDeltaWrite verifies the carried bytes against the size and digest the change declares before writing, and refuses a change that declares no digest at all.
validateDeltaContents refuses a sensitive path without the opt-in, a deleted path that carries content, and content that disagrees with the declared digest.
validateNoUnreferencedDeltaContent refuses content in the map that no change names, so bytes cannot travel under a name the change list does not mention.
The package's own test states the conflict rule the implementation must honour and that it must not acquire a second answer.

interface.types: stow.DeltaDocument{Version, BaseID, TargetID, Created, Changes []stow.DeltaChange, Files, Bytes, Content map[string][]byte, IncludeSensitive} is the transferable form; stow.DeltaChange{Path, Kind, From, To *stow.CheckpointFile} is one path's difference. stow.DeltaOptions{MaxBytes, MaxFiles, IncludeSensitive, Encoded, ExpectSHA256} bounds and binds the document. The four refusals are named values: stow.ErrDeltaConflict, stow.ErrDeltaVersionUnsupported, stow.ErrDeltaTooLarge and stow.ErrDeltaDigestMismatch. The entry points are stow.CreateDelta, stow.EncodeDelta, stow.DecodeDelta, stow.DeltaDocumentDigest, stow.VerifyDeltaDigest, stow.ApplyDelta, stow.ApplyDeltaWithOptions and stow.ReadCheckpointFile.
invariants: A delta names both ends, so a receiver can check it is being applied where it thinks it is; both ids must be valid checkpoint ids and both checkpoints must belong to the same workspace (pkg/stow/delta.go:185, pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:35).
The content is on the wire, base64 under its own name; a document without content is describable but not applicable (pkg/stow/delta.go:130).

Every change carries the from and to CheckpointFile records (path, size, mode and sha256), so the receiver can assert the precondition against the whole recorded state before touching anything (pkg/stow/delta.go:147, pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:35).
The change kinds are the same vocabulary the checkpoint diff already uses, so a delta does not acquire a second dialect (pkg/stow/delta.go:45, pkg/stow/checkpoint.go:402).
Every precondition is checked before any byte is written, so a refused application leaves the target exactly as it was (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:21, pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:63).
A change that carries content must declare a digest for it; the omission is refused rather than tolerated (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:163).
The document's declared totals must agree with its actual content and change count, or it is malformed (pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:22).
Content that no change names is refused, and a deleted path that carries content is refused (pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:61, pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:90).
Applying a delta produces a new checkpoint with a new id and refuses to replace an existing one (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:267).
error_modes: stow.ErrDeltaConflict when the target's copy of a changed path diverges from the from-state (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:201), when a deleted path diverges from the from-state (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:193), when an added path already exists (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:187), when a deleted path does not exist (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:191), or when a changed path does not exist (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:199).
stow.ErrDeltaVersionUnsupported when the document's version is not the one this build speaks (pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:33).
stow.ErrDeltaTooLarge when the document declares or carries more than MaxDeltaBytes (pkg/stow/delta.go:417, pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:81).
stow.ErrDeltaDigestMismatch when the encoded bytes do not hash to the digest the sender published (pkg/stow/delta.go:383).
"stow: delta crosses workspaces: %q and %q" when the two checkpoints belong to different workspaces (pkg/stow/delta.go:186).

"stow: delta transport does not support portable object checkpoints" on the create side (pkg/stow/delta.go:183) and "stow: portable object checkpoints do not support deltas" on the apply side (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:57).

"stow: delta change %q has unknown kind %q" for a kind outside added, changed and deleted on the apply side (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:114); validation refuses the same class with "stow: invalid delta change %q" (pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:110).
"stow: delta carries no content for %q" when a change needs bytes the document does not carry (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:134, pkg/stow/delta_validation.go:70).
ordering: The digest check comes before the decode on the receiving side, so a document altered in transit is refused on that ground rather than on whatever the alteration happened to break (cmd/stow-s3/workspace_delta.go:125, cmd/stow-s3/workspace_delta.go:128).

On the apply side the document and digest are validated, then the base is loaded, then the lock is taken and the base is loaded again, then the preconditions are checked, then the staging directory is created (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:35, pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:39, pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:47, pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:52, pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:63, pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:69).
The staged tree starts as a copy of the base and the changes are replayed over it, so a replay only has to express what differs (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:80).
The published checkpoint is scanned and re-described from the staged files directory, not from the stage itself, so the manifest matches the layout the loader expects (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:256).
The registry admission check runs before the publish, so a delta that would exceed a retention cap is refused before a checkpoint id is consumed (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:280).
configuration: MaxBytes and MaxFiles bound a delta; zero takes the same defaults as the archive path so a delta and an archive of the same work are accepted or refused together (pkg/stow/delta.go:54, pkg/stow/delta.go:306, pkg/stow/checkpoint_archive.go:27).
IncludeSensitive carries the paths the sensitive-name guard would otherwise refuse, on the same opt-in the archive path requires (pkg/stow/delta.go:110).

Encoded and ExpectSHA256 bind the received bytes to the sender's published digest; the pair is optional because a receiver with no trusted copy of the digest cannot invent one (pkg/stow/delta.go:112, pkg/stow/delta.go:120).

MaxDeltaBytes is the format's own ceiling, 16 MiB, and it is exported so a caller reading a delta from a source it does not control can bound the read itself (pkg/stow/delta.go:61, pkg/stow/delta.go:65).

implementation: CreateDelta (pkg/stow/delta.go:160) validates the options, loads both manifests, refuses a portable checkpoint and refuses a delta that crosses workspaces, takes a capture lock for the workspace and reloads both manifests under it so the comparison is against a stable pair. recordDeltaChanges (pkg/stow/delta.go:229) indexes both file sets, walks the sorted union of their paths and hands each to recordChange, which decides added, changed or deleted by comparing the digests and modes, and attaches the bytes of an added or changed path through attach. attach re-reads the bytes out of the target checkpoint and verifies them against the digest the manifest recorded, and refuses a sensitive-looking path unless the caller opted in. enforceBounds runs after every path, so a document that would exceed the caller's cap is refused as it is built rather than after it is complete. EncodeDelta validates the document before serialising it, and DeltaDocumentDigest digests exactly the bytes EncodeDelta produced. DecodeDelta bounds the raw read at 32 MiB before parsing, validates the document and then checks the size it actually carries. VerifyDeltaDigest is a no-op when the expected digest is empty, because failing closed there would make the option mandatory in every call. ApplyDeltaWithOptions (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:31) validates the document and the digest, loads the base, takes the mutation-capture lock, refuses a portable base, verifies every precondition against the base's current contents, stages a copy of the base's files, replays the changes over it, and publishes a new checkpoint by rename. The verification of a change's content happens per write and before the write, so a document that was altered in transit cannot change a working set without changing what it claims to change.

callers.scope: The CLI's `workspace delta` verb calls stow.CreateDelta, encodes it and publishes the digest the receiver is expected to hand back.
The `workspace apply` verb verifies the digest before it decodes, so a document altered in transit is refused on the digest rather than on whatever the alteration broke.
The same verb then calls stow.ApplyDeltaWithOptions, the module's application entry point.
The CLI translates the four named delta refusals into operator-readable messages and leaves everything else alone, which is a caller that depends on the error vocabulary being stable.
The CLI's end-to-end test drives the delta and apply verbs across two registries, including the portable-archive hand-off of the base.
The package's own test exercises the conflict rule, the wire round trip and the same-vocabulary requirement.
A test drives ApplyDeltaWithOptions with the Encoded/ExpectSHA256 pair and pins the substitution the document digest exists to stop.
A test calls VerifyDeltaDigest directly to pin the case-insensitive, trimmed comparison and the empty-digest no-op.
A test exercises the create/encode/decode/apply round trip, a traversal attempt and a same-length corruption refusal.
A test asserts CreateDelta refuses portable object checkpoints.

depth_assessment.deletion_test: The complexity concentrates in the callers. Deleting this module would push the conflict rule, the digest rule and the ordering rule into the transport that carries a delta: that a target which is neither the from-state nor the to-state must be refused rather than merged (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:182), that the per-file digests do not bind the change list so the whole document's digest must be checked (pkg/stow/delta.go:364), and that every precondition must be checked before any byte is written (pkg/stow/delta_apply.go:61). A caller re-implementing any of these would produce a delta that applies cleanly against a target it was never written for, which is the failure the module's own comment names as invisible (pkg/stow/delta.go:91). The production caller set is one file, so the re-implemented complexity would land in one place rather than many, but it would still have to be re-derived from scratch, which is what keeps the verdict deep rather than a pass-through.

leverage: A caller exchanges the difference rather than the tree, and gets the conflict rule, the digest binding and the atomic application for free. A sender publishes one digest and a receiver checks it once; the receiver does not have to reason about which bytes were altered. A caller that applies a delta gets a new checkpoint rather than a mutated base, so a failed application is invisible to the target.
locality: The document format lives in pkg/stow/delta.go, the application in pkg/stow/delta_apply.go and the validation in pkg/stow/delta_validation.go.
